===== [p61-61] MODEL 7AF > VACUUM (2块) =====
--[p61]-- With such a system, the unit drain may be connected to the industrial waste drain [A] and the unit vacuum supply connected to the vacuum clean dry air [J].
The connections for left work chuck vacuum [E1], right work chuck vacuum [E2], and robot vacuum [E3] are 1/2-inch tubes located at the lower rear of the machine.
A bulkhead fitting is provided to connect the system to facility plumbing. The plumbing should be selected to provide the necessary flow and pressure for the machine.
--[p61]-- VACUUM
The vacuum connection to the machine will collect a significant amount of process water and silicon particles through the vacuum line to the vacuum source. An isolated vacuum pump with a self-contained drain system is available from Strasbaugh as a machine option. For use with a facility vacuum supply, a wall-mountable vacuum/waste separator is also available.

===== [p179-179] MENUS USED IN BASIC OPERATION > WHILE THE CYCLE IS RUNNING, MONITOR THE STATUS SCREEN DISPLAY VALUES (1块) =====
--[p179]-- WHILE THE CYCLE IS RUNNING, MONITOR THE STATUS SCREEN DISPLAY VALUES
20. During the processing of the wafers, monitor the real time display and compare with the following requirements:
a. Chuck vacuum during grinding must be greater than 18 inches of mercury.
b. Motor current for the fine and coarse spindles must be less than 9.4 amps.
c. Left and right probe fluctuation must be less than 5 microns.
d. Coarse spindle force must not rise above 60 lbs. for more than 5 seconds.
e.
Fine spindle force must not rise above 60 lbs. for more than 5 seconds.
f. Fine and coarse spindle force must fluctuate less than 10 lbs.

===== [p120-120] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > POWER UP (3块) =====
--[p120]-- POWER UP
Refer to the engineering drawings for the following description of power up circuitry. The basic functions of the power up circuit are to maintain closure of circuit paths 1L1, 1L2, and 1L3 after the Machine On pushbutton is depressed and to break the circuit path if a "fault" is sensed. To maintain the circuit path means to "hold down" the main contactor, 1CON. When the Machine On button is depressed, a set of contacts is closed, and the solenoid of 1CON is energized.
--[p120]-- When the solenoid of 1CON is energized, it closes the contacts for 1L1, 1L2, and 1L3, providing power throughout the machine.
A fault occurs if a single service door interlock (see Interlock section) is open or if the user depresses either of the two Emergency Off pushbuttons (EMO). The Emergency Off pushbuttons are the Main Control Panel EMO and the Rear EMO.
--[p120]-- When a fault occurs, power is removed from the main contactor's solenoid, and the contacts for the three arterial power lines, 1L1, 1L2, and 1L3 and for terminals 13 and 14, are opened, removing power from throughout the machine.

===== [p41-41] MODEL 7AF > STEP 1 - UNPACKING/INSPECTION (2块) =====
--[p41]-- STEP 1 - UNPACKING/INSPECTION
The Model 7AF Wafer Grinder is shipped from the factory in one unified section--with the grinding area and wafer handling area bolted together in the machine operation configuration. The handling section is attached to the grinding section by a hinge at the left side of the machine and two 3/8-16 setscrew/wing nut sets located at the right side of the machine, as viewed from the front.
--[p41]-- The machine is wrapped in one or more layers of plastic (to prevent contamination during shipping) and fastened to a shipping pallet. Before unpacking the machine from its shipping provisions, inspect the exterior carefully for any indication of possible shipping damage. If such signs exist, contact the shipper to report a claim and obtain additional instructions before proceeding.
For details on the machine cabinet and the door numbering system, refer to the Physical Description chapter of this manual.

===== [p129-129] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > WATER SYSTEM (3块) =====
--[p129]-- Note: When monitoring spindle coolant IN and/or OUT pressures with a flow switch, the system should be setup with a minimum 15 psi difference between the incoming and outgoing spindle coolant pressures. The outgoing spindle coolant pressure will always be LESS than the incoming spindle coolant pressure.
--[p129]-- WATER SYSTEM
The water system is comprised of two subsystems, D.I. (deionized water) and municipal or temperature-controlled water, all detailed on the engineering drawings labeled 118168F\_ (fluids). Refer also to the Pneumatic Adjustments chapter of this manual for details on water use and related valve panels.
In the grinding area, D.I. water (deionized water) is used to supply water to the left and right work chucks. In the handling area, D.I. water is supplied to the spin-rinse station.
--[p129]-- The inhouse D.I. water supply enters at the rear of the machine where it is distributed via a manifold and 1/2-in. tubing throughout the rest of the machine.
The municipal or temperature-controlled water supply enters the machine at the rear; it is then routed to a manifold where it is used to cool the motors of the four air bearing spindles. Green tubing carries the cooling water in; yellow tubing carries the cooling water out.

===== [p128-128] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > VACUUM SYSTEM (4块) =====
--[p128]-- The vacuum connection to the machine will collect a significant amount of process water and silicon particles through the vacuum line to the vacuum source. An isolated vacuum pump with a self-contained drain system is available from Strasbaugh as a machine option. For use with a facility vacuum supply, a wall-mountable vacuum/waste separator is also available.
--[p128]-- VACUUM SYSTEM
Refer to the engineering drawings labeled 118168P\_ (pneumatic) and 118168A\_ (assembly) as well as the Pneumatic Adjustments chapter of this manual for details on vacuum use and related valve panels.
The vacuum system controls the vacuum source needed to secure the wafers to the work chucks, the spin-rinse station, the pre-aligner, and the robot end effector. The inhouse vacuum source, which enters from the rear of the machine, must be an average of 22 inches of mercury.
--[p128]-- Normally open valves are used on all wafer chucks to prevent the release of wafers in the event of a loss of power. When the solenoid of a wafer valve is de-energized, air pilot pressure forces the valve's diaphragm down to divert vacuum to the cylinder port. Air pilot pressure must be available to move the diaphragm. When the solenoid is energized, the air pilot source is cut off, allowing the spring to return the diaphragm and close off the vacuum source.
--[p128]-- Analog vacuum sensors on the work chucks and spin-rinse station and vacuum switches on the pre-aligner and robot test to see if vacuum is in the line, indicating that a wafer is attached. Whenever a solenoid is deenergized to release a wafer, the blow-off solenoid energizes, routing air into the vacuum lines to release the grip upon the wafer (excluding the pre-aligner which is vented to atmosphere).

===== [p112-112] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > SERVO AMPLIFIER (3块) =====
--[p112]-- In response to the velocity command input, the amplifier module uses pulse width modulation for exciting the motor windings, to ramp the motor up or down to constant velocity. Encoder signals provide information regarding the motor's absolute position and velocity.
--[p112]-- Each amplifier module chassis is supplied with 110 VAC which creates a 170 VDC power supply. The motor is enabled when the inhibit line input of the amplifier module is high. The inhibit line input is turned on and off by a digital output controlled by the machine’s control computer.
The amplifier module receives an analog velocity command signal from the servo channel of the motion control board.
--[p112]-- SERVO AMPLIFIER
Refer to engineering drawings labeled 118168E\_ (electrical) and 118168L (logic/software) for the following discussion. For each of the six DC motors discussed above in the Servo Control section, an amplifier module communicates between the motion control board and the brushless DC servo motor. The amplifier modules are identified as 1BSC, 2BSC, 3BSC, 6BSC, 7BSC, and 8BSC for axes 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, and 8, respectively (axes 4 and 5 are AC).

===== [p106-106] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > SPIN-RINSE STATION (3块) =====
--[p106]-- SPIN-RINSE STATION
Note: The times included in the description below are approximate--all times are process-oriented and variable.
With the spin-rinse station's spindle in up position, the robot releases the wafer onto the spindle. Vacuum is then turned on at the vacuum chuck in preparation for holding the wafer in place. The spindle then lowers down into the pan.
When the spindle moves down, a programmable variable speed servo motor turns on, rotating the wafer.
--[p106]-- During cleaning the spindle rotates at a relatively low RPM; during drying it rotates at approximately 4000 RPM.
After cleaning and drying, the lid retracts up, the chuck moves up, and vacuum is turned off, releasing the wafer. The robot then picks up the wafer.
--[p106]-- Lowered by a pneumatic cylinder, the lid moves down. The lid contains two D.I. water nozzles and a small articulated bristle brush. The two D.I. water nozzles spray for ten seconds, cleaning grinding residue off the wafer. The brush then moves from the edge of the wafer to its center and back and forth. After cleaning, clean dry air or nitrogen is blown on the wafer during the spin dry segment of the cycle to accelerate drying.

===== [p82-82] MODEL 7AF > Notes on the Turret Assemblies: (3块) =====
--[p82]-- Notes on the Turret Assemblies:
• Two adjacent cassette assemblies cannot be accessed at the same time.
• Wafers are loaded in cassettes device-side up.
The Spin-Rinse Station (15) moves a brush from the center to the edge of the wafer, rinses the wafer with D. I. water, and spins the wafer up to 4000 RPM until dry.
The Robot (16) is equipped with a rotating wrist and a single vacuum chuck end effector to permit picking the wafer up from either the bottom or top as needed.
--[p82]-- The following is a summary of the sequence of robot movements in relation to other machine movements:
1. wafer is picked up at send cassette device-side up
2. wafer is flipped
3. wafer is set on the pre-aligner
4. wafer is picked up device-side down
5. wafer is placed on work chuck device-side down
6. wafer is ground
7. wafer is picked up, still device-side down
8. wafer is taken to spin-rinse for cleaning of the ground surface
9. wafer is picked up device-side down
10.
--[p82]-- robot wrist rotates to present wafer to receive cassette device-side up
The robot travels in a circular motion with approximately 350 degrees of motion (a dead zone exists at the front center of the machine). The robot has Z, radial, and theta motion.

===== [p218-218] OPERATOR DAILY PREVENTIVEMAINTENANCE SCHEDULE > GRINDING SEQUENCE (5块) =====
--[p218]-- Grind Sequence Segment | Description
Note: The air cut depth provides a margin of error to prevent rapid feeding down to the wafer surface itself.
Grinding | Grinding is divided into the steps shown below:
Step 1 | During step 1, the wafer is ground from its original wafer thickness to the step 1 target thickness goal at the step 1 programmed feedrate and work chuck speed specified by the recipe.
--[p218 [表]]-- GRINDING SEQUENCE
The 7AF grinding sequence for both coarse and fine grind is divided into the segments shown below. Five segments (grinding step 1, grinding step 2, grinding step 3, dwell, and lift) are programmable at the Wafer Recipes menu.
Grind Sequence Segment | Description
Home | The grind wheel is initially in its home position, which is at the upper limit switch, a minimum of 6 mm above the chuck surface.
--[p218]-- Step 2 | During step 2, the wafer is ground from the wafer thickness achieved upon completion of step 1 to the step 2 target thickness goal at the step 2 programmed feedrate and work chuck speed specified by the recipe.
Step 3 | During step 3, the wafer is ground from the wafer thickness achieved upon completion of step 2 to the step 3 target thickness goal at the step 3 programmed feedrate and work chuck speed specified by the recipe.
--[p218]-- Dwell | The step 3 thickness goal is the finished work thickness. During the dwell segment the grind wheel height is kept unchanged while the work chuck rotates the number of revolutions specified by
Lift | the recipe at the dwell segment programmed speed. After completion of the dwell segment, the grind wheel is allowed to lift at a rate (in
Rapid Feed | microns per second) specified by the recipe to a height (in microns) specified by the recipe.
After the grind wheel has withdrawn from the wafer by the amount specified for lift, it is rapidly fed back to its travel height.
--[p218]-- Travel Height | When the grind cycle starts, the wheel is rapidly fed to a travel height, which is 2000 microns above the tallest chuck. This is the height at which the grind wheels are located as the bridge travels to each of its three positions.
Rapid Feed | When the bridge is in position, the wheel is rapidly fed to a height equal to the measured wafer thickness plus a pre-determined "air cut" depth.

===== [p208-208] OPERATOR DAILY PREVENTIVEMAINTENANCE SCHEDULE > NEEDS ASSISTANCE: YELLOW FLASHING, ALARM SOUNDS (2块) =====
--[p208]-- NEEDS ASSISTANCE: YELLOW FLASHING, ALARM SOUNDS
Each time the "Operator Instruction" message is displayed on the control computer screen (requesting operator attention to move the machine into the next state or to offer information) the tower light will change to flashing yellow within five seconds of the screen’s display of the message. The five second delay before the light begins flashing and the alarm begins sounding permits the operator to respond before the alarm sounds.
--[p208]-- Acknowledging the request by touching a button or an inactive portion of the menu screen will clear the "Operator Instruction" message from the screen and clear the "Needs Assistance" state.
End of cycle reached and dressing disk replacement requests are examples of this state.

===== [p118-119] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > AC DISTRIBUTION (4块) =====
--[p119]-- The three duplex receptacles are AC outlets providing power for the control computer (inside door 7), the robot and pre-aligner controllers (inside door 10), and the display monitor at the front top of the machine.
Transformer 3T is a step down transformer providing 120 VAC power to six servo amplifier modules (1BSC through 6BSC).
Inline circuit breakers protect each of the three transformers, 1T, 2T, and 3T, on both the primary and secondary circuits.
Circuit breakers also protect individual parallel branch circuits on the secondary side of transformer 2T.
--[p118]-- AC DISTRIBUTION
The required inhouse electrical power is three-phase, 208 VAC,
45 amperes. Inhouse electrical power terminates to the main power circuit breaker 1CB. The circuit breaker is a single throw, 45-amp rated circuit breaker. From the main power circuit breaker, wires 1L1, 1L2, and 1L3 carry AC electrical power to the contacts of the main contactor. From the main power circuit breaker, AC power branches out to transformer 1T via wires 1L2 and 1L3.
--[p119]-- Terminal strip 8TS branches out three-phase, 208 VAC power to each of the two variable frequency AC grind spindle rotational drives and single-phase 208 VAC power to transformer 3T and transformer 2T.
Transformer 2T is a step down transformer providing single-phase 120 VAC power to three DC voltage power supplies, 1PS, 2PS, and 3PS, and to three 120 VAC duplex receptacles.
--[p118]-- Transformer 1T is a step down transformer providing 24 VAC for the power up circuit and interlocks, described in the Power Up and Interlock sections of this chapter, below.
The main contactor completes the three major arterial wires 2L1, 2L2, and 2L3 to provide three-phase AC electrical power throughout the remainder of the machine. AC electrical power is branched from the three major arterial wires to individual subassemblies and components by terminal strip 8TS.

===== [p102-102] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > LEFT/RIGHT WORK CHUCKS (3块) =====
--[p102]-- Vacuum is used to retain the wafer during grinding, and air is used for blowoff to aid in releasing the wafer. D.I. water, used during conditioning, cleans the vacuum pores by blowing water through them, helping to ensure good vacuum for the next wafer.
--[p102]-- LEFT/RIGHT WORK CHUCKS
Each work chuck spindle is an air bearing (see below) spindle mounted to one of the side plates of the bed. The work chuck spindles are functionally and structurally very similar to the coarse and fine (upper) spindles, with the exception that the upper spindles are designed to rotate at faster speeds than the lower (work chuck) spindles.
Each work chuck assembly is bolted to its associated spindle; vacuum used for wafer retention is routed through the ceramic chuck.
--[p102]-- The ceramic chuck is mounted to the backing plate, and the unit is bolted to the mounting plate which attaches directly to the air bearing and acts as a coupler to retain the work chuck. Note that the work chuck spindles provide rotational motion only (no vertical or horizontal motion). Lines for vacuum/air blowoff and D.I. water/backflush run through a hole in the center of each work chuck spindle.

===== [p243-243] RECIPE PARAMETER SETTINGS AND INFORMATION AVAILABLE AT THE WHEEL AND CHUCK RECIPES MENU > PRE-ALIGNER SECOND FLAT SENSING – OPTION (2块) =====
--[p243]-- Under normal circumstances the sensor will expect to find the minor flat 90 degrees clockwise from the major flat, however, the software will accommodate an offset to allow sensing the minor flat at other locations. The software release notes (distributed with the machine software) will contain additional information concerning the adjustment of this option.
10
--[p243]-- PRE-ALIGNER SECOND FLAT SENSING – OPTION
This option provides the capability to sense the second or “minor” flat of a wafer and thereby determine if the wafer has been loaded with the correct side facing upward. This option can also flip the wafer over if it does not sense the minor flat, and then recheck that the minor flat is in the correct position. This option only works with 3 inch to 4.25 inch wafers, and the micrometer sensor adjustment must be reset with each change in wafer diameter.

===== [p130-130] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > EXHAUST SYSTEM (2块) =====
--[p130]-- From the plenum exhaust tubes connect to the left grind chamber, the right grind chamber, and the spin-rinse station. The exhaust system prevents the buildup of vapors during the grinding process and exhausts airborne particles from the grinding process.
--[p130]-- EXHAUST SYSTEM
Refer to the engineering drawings labeled 118168F\_ (fluids) and 118168A\_ (assembly) for further details.
The exhaust system consists of hoses, a plenum located in the handling section of the machine between the robot and the grinding chamber, and a connection to an inhouse exhaust source. A five-inch collar at the rear of the machine connects to the inhouse exhaust source. A single five-inch diameter tube runs from the rear of the machine to the plenum.

Volume(s) | Contents

===== [p105-105] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > PRE-ALIGNER (3块) =====
--[p105]-- PRE-ALIGNER
The Equipe Technologies pre-aligner centers the wafer and aligns the notch or flat (usually notch for eight-inch wafers and flat for six-inch wafers) using optical sensing and a closed loop servo driven three-axis mechanism. During alignment the wafer can be raised and lowered, moved radially, and rotated around a center axis. The mechanism first rotates the incoming wafer over a linear array CCD sensor.
--[p105]-- The CCD sensor, with an associated uniform light source, provides data to the separate controller box and its internal computer over a parallel I/O link. The controller box computer then analyses the data and computes a vector of offset for the wafer to place the wafer in a position concentric to the chuck.
The pre-aligner is equipped with vacuum pins around the rotating chuck which move up and down to lift the wafer in an "x" direction to shift the wafer's center position.
--[p105]-- The vector of offset is aligned with the directional movement of the pins which move up to perform the offset.
The pre-aligner then moves the primary flat or notch back over the sensor for a high resolution scan after which the center of the flat or notch is moved to the user specified position. The pre-aligner signals when alignment is complete and the wafer is ready to be picked up by the robot.

===== [p450-450] ROBOT (AND PRE-ALIGNER) SETUP AND CALIBRATION > RSR (1块) =====
--[p450]-- RSR
Returns the wafer count from the last performed scan. The information will be displayed in the form of a 25-digit number such as "0100100000000000000200001". Each individual digit represents a slot in the cassette with the first digit assigned to slot 1 and the last to slot 25. If a slot is designated as "0", the slot is empty. If the slot is designated as "1", a wafer is present. A slot designation of "2" indicates that a wafer has been cross-slotted.

===== [p207-207] OPERATOR DAILY PREVENTIVEMAINTENANCE SCHEDULE > LIGHT TOWER OPERATION (1块) =====
--[p207]-- LIGHT TOWER OPERATION
The light tower provides visible and audible indications of the machine state. The color of the light, whether or not the light is flashing, and the presence or absence of an audible alarm all aid in communicating machine status to the operator. The information below details possible machine states, their indicators, and suggested immediate actions to be taken in response to the states.

===== [p113-113] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > I/O AND INTERFACE SYSTEM (4块) =====
--[p113]-- They are individually listed and identified with accompanying part numbers on the engineering drawings. All five I/O mounting racks and the interface adapter card inside the control computer are chained together with a single 50 conductor ribbon cable. This establishes a communication bus line between all I/O mounting racks and the control computer. The control software makes all decisions and instructions concerning the individual I/O points.
The brain boards of the mounting racks implement the instructions.
--[p113]-- Digital inputs are such switches and sensors as the control panel push buttons and limit switches. Analog inputs and outputs are used for devices that have a range of values represented by varying voltage or current levels. A high speed interface adapter card resides in one expansion slot of the control computer. It interfaces the computer motherboard to the I/O bus, allowing input and output instructions from the control computer for a specific I/O point.
--[p113]-- I/O AND INTERFACE SYSTEM
The I/O and interface system hardware used in the machine form an industry standard optically isolated I/O system. This system incorporates brain boards, driver modules, and a host computer interface card to read or drive all digital and analog signals. Digital inputs are 24 volt DC; outputs are 24 volt DC. Digital outputs are used to turn on or off solenoids and enable servo amplifiers throughout the machine.
--[p113]-- Shown in the engineering drawings, there are a total of five I/O racks. Four racks are mounted on the pull out shelf above the control computer (behind door 7); the single analog rack is mounted behind door 8. They are identified as digital or analog inputs and outputs. Each I/O mounting rack has a brain board. The I/O mounting racks hold the individual I/O driver modules; several types of driver module types are used on these racks.

===== [p114-115] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > ROBOT AND CONTROLLER, PRE-ALIGNER AND CONTROLLER (6块) =====
--[p115]-- The pre-aligner is used as a subsystem to the robot; the primary RS-232 port (COM 1) of the pre-aligner controller is connected to the COM 2 port of the robot's controller. When daisy-chained, the robot's controller will act as a master, and the pre-aligner controller will be the slave. All data is sent to the primary port of the robot controller (DB 25 connector located on the CPU card).
--[p114]-- The pre-aligner is equipped with vacuum pins around the rotating chuck. The pins can move up and down to lift the wafer and in an "X" direction to shift the wafer's center position. The vector of offset for the wafer is then lined up with the directional movement of the pins, which move up to perform the offset. The pre-aligner then moves the primary flat or notch back over the sensor for a high resolution scan. It then moves the center of the flat or notch to the user specified position.
--[p114]-- The pre-aligner consists of a servo driven three-axis mechanism which first rotates the incoming wafer over a linear array CCD sensor. The CCD sensor, with an associated uniform light source, provides data to the separate controller box and its internal PC computer over a parallel input/output link. The computer in the controller then analyzes this data and computes a vector of offset for the wafer to permit positioning of the wafer concentrically on the chuck.
--[p115]-- A macro being executed by the main controller (that of the robot) can also send a command to the second controller (that of the pre-aligner) and send and receive data accordingly. The system host controller transmits software commands using ASCII strings to the robot via the DB 25 male connector RS-232 serial port located on the CPU card at the back of the Equipe Smart Controller box. The 7AF's control computer's communication to the robot and pre-aligner is via its serial port (COM 1).
--[p114]-- ROBOT AND CONTROLLER, PRE-ALIGNER AND CONTROLLER
The Equipe Technologies robot and controller and pre-aligner and controller packages incorporate closed loop DC servo motor control and precision mechanics for wafer handling with full servo control of the radial, theta, and Z axes.
The robot's radial motion extends and retracts the robot arm through a center point; its theta motion rotates the arm around the center point; its Z motion raises and lowers the arm.
--[p114]-- The pre-aligner's radial motion centers the wafer; its theta motion rotates the chuck;   
its Z motion raises and lowers the pins.
The PC-based controller permits the robot to make intelligent decisions based upon its environment utilizing 16 standard external I/O's. The open software structure allows intelligent macros to be stored in the controller. A "PUT" command is given to the robot to place a wafer. Likewise, a "GET" command is given to tell the robot to get the wafer.

===== [p451-451] ROBOT (AND PRE-ALIGNER) SETUP AND CALIBRATION > SCSI [STATION],[VARIABLE #],[VALUE] (1块) =====
--[p451]-- SCSI [STATION],[VARIABLE #],[VALUE]
A set of variables associated with each station instructs the robot on handling the scanning data and end effector orientation for that station. The command "SCSI B,5,23" would set the current value of variable number 5 for station B at 23.

===== [p63-63] MODEL 7AF > AIR BEARING SPINDLE MOTOR COOLING WATER IN/OUT (2块) =====
--[p63]-- AIR BEARING SPINDLE MOTOR COOLING WATER IN/OUT
The air bearing spindle motor cooling water in, spindle coolant in [F], may be connected to the municipal water supply or to chilled municipal water through a 3/8- inch tube connection at the lower rear of the machine.
The air bearing spindle motor cooling water out, spindle coolant out [G], connection is also made through a 3/8-inch tube connection at the lower rear of the machine.
--[p63]-- Note: When monitoring coolant in and/or out pressures with a flow switch, the system should be setup with a minimum 15 psi difference between the incoming spindle coolant and the outgoing spindle coolant pressures. The outgoing spindle coolant pressure will always be less than the incoming spindle coolant pressure.

The home (index) position for the work and spin chucks is only set when a "Home All" function is performed in the Home Screen. The spin chuck uses home index hardware (sensors) that will index the chuck in the same place in all cases. The work chuck checks for a home index and uses this for a reference, if the OPTIONAL hardware is installed on the machine.

The work chucks, however, can operate without the hardware by disconnecting the sensor and setting the Machine Variables 10 and 11 to 0.0, as outlined below for Machines Without Home Index Hardware Installed.

===== [p28-28] ABOUT THIS MANUAL > MECHANICAL COMPONENTS (4块) =====
--[p28]-- Inflatable seals envelope each grind chamber, capturing vapor and particles which are exhausted out via a plenum.
The wafer handling area is an assembly designed to provide a safe and convenient method for robotic loading and unloading of wafers. Rotary actuators under each of the four cassette platforms rotate the cassettes 180 ° to present them to the robot or the operator. A pre-aligner orients the wafer before grinding; after grinding a spin-rinse station cleans and dries the wafer.
Mechanical, electrical, and software interlocks provide complete user safety for all machine operations.
--[p28]-- Single work chuck wafer stationing for stock removal and finish grinding diminishes the chance of damaging or breaking the wafer through additional handling or placing the wafer on a contaminated chuck. The height of the work chuck is checked at the beginning of a grind cycle and intermittently as the process requires (in case the chuck heats and rises) to assure accuracy in grinding. Probe measurement of the wafer is relative to the height of the work chuck.
--[p28]-- The two air bearing coarse and fine grind upper spindles are functionally identical and designated as coarse or fine only by the type of diamond wheel installed. The upper spindles are enclosed within a bridge which travels linearly to alternately or simultaneously coarse and fine grind the product.
The two air bearing work (lower) spindles and their support mechanisms are mechanically identical. The 8 1/4-inch diameter ceramic work chucks may be used with both six and eight-inch wafers.
--[p28]-- MECHANICAL COMPONENTS
The machine consists of two major mechanical components (the grinding area and the wafer handling area), each enclosed within separate machine cabinet sections which detach for easy access to internal components. Together the cabinet sections form a grind area and protective user enclosure to provide a sturdy, safe and clean grinding process:
• The grinding section of the machine encompasses four air bearing spindles.

===== [p122-122] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > Effects of Opening Doors (2块) =====
--[p122]-- Effects of Opening Doors
Opening door 10, 17, 18, or 20 at any time shuts power down to the entire machine, including the control computer. Recover by manually clearing any leftover wafers, powering up and rehoming the machine.
Opening door 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, or 19 during an auto grind cycle terminates the cycle and inhibits the servos. Recover by manually clearing any leftover wafers and restarting the auto cycle.
Opening door 7, 8, or 9 has no effect on machine power or the cycle running.
--[p122]-- Opening door 5 or 6 halts the cycle; closing doors 5 and 6 resumes the cycle. (Their function is similar to that of the Halt Cycle button on the Grind Cycle menu.)

Figure 3-6 Control Panel
The white MACHINE ON lamp, located at the left side of the panel, glows when the machine is on.

--[p30]-- SAFETY
The Model 7AF Wafer Grinder has been designed for safe operation. However, caution should be exercised while operating this machine. Failure to adhere to the following safety instructions and to good safety practices may result in injury to personnel or damage to the machine.

===== [p106-106] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > SEND 1, SEND 2, RECEIVE 1, RECEIVE 2 CASSETTE ACCESSTURRET ASSEMBLIES (2块) =====
--[p106]-- SEND 1, SEND 2, RECEIVE 1, RECEIVE 2 CASSETTE ACCESSTURRET ASSEMBLIES
The four cassette turret assemblies are functionally identical. A selection at the touch screen of the control computer monitor requests rotation of each platform. The rotary actuator under the cassette turret rotates the turret platform 180°, smoothly presenting the cassette to the robot or to the operator. The cassette platform can accommodate cassettes for three-inch to eight-inch wafers with no mechanical adjustments.
--[p106]-- A sensor indicates cassette presence or absence. Note that two adjacent cassette turret assemblies cannot be accessed at the same time.
(This page intentionally left blank)

===== [p53-55] MODEL 7AF > Side to Side (3块) =====
--[p53]-- Side to Side
1. Confirm that the handling section is loosely joined to the grinding section of the machine:
If needed, slightly loosen the two wing nuts of the two fastening setscrew and wing nut pairs securing the grinding section of the machine to the handling section by rotating them counterclockwise manually.
2.
--[p53]-- Place a standard bubble level side to side (one end of the level pointing toward the right side of the machine and one end pointing toward the left side) on the robot well (black aluminum casting).
3. Open door 10.
4. Adjust the alignment leg (cam follower ball bearing) located at the right side of the machine and extending from the handling section to the grinding section:
a. Using a 5/8-in. open end or socket wrench, rotate the two 3/8-in.
--[p55]-- hex head hold down bolts counterclockwise to loosen them.
b. Using a 5/8-in. open end wrench, loosen the four 3/8-in. locking nuts by rotating them counterclockwise.
c. Using a 3/16-in. hex key, rotate the adjusting bolts clockwise or counterclockwise as needed to achieve a level reading.
Notes:
Rotating the adjusting screw clockwise raises the right side of the handling section.
Rotating the adjusting screw counterclockwise lowers the right side of the handling section.
d.
When the reading is level, retighten the locking nuts.
e. Retighten the hold down bolts.

===== [p289-290] MECHANICAL MAINTENANCE > Left Spindle Fringe Plate (3块) =====
--[p289]-- Left Spindle Fringe Plate
1. Manually move the bridge by rotating the bridge sprocket until the upper left spindle is centered over the lower left spindle and the upper right spindle is centered over the lower right spindle.
CAUTION: Always confirm that the digital probes are in up position before moving the bridge to avoid breaking them off!
2. Demount the left digital probe and remount it to the upper left spindle:
a. Using a 5/32-in.

--[p290]-- hex key and one of the 1/4-20 bolts (from the bolt and nut pairs included in the fringe plate tool kit) mount the probe fixture to any one of the six holes in the upper left spindle grinding wheel backing plate.
Position the probe such that the probe bellows is as close to the backing plate as possible without touching it.

===== [p101-101] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > COARSE/FINE SPINDLES (4块) =====
--[p101]-- The drive assembly is a recirculating ball lead screw support, with the ball screw driving the spindle up and down. Within the coupling between the ball screw and the assembly that moves the spindle up and down, a load cell is installed to measure the spindle weight. The information from the load cell is used to determine the amount of down force applied to the wafer.
--[p101]-- The counterbalance assembly also has a load cell to read the counterbalance required.
Hard stops and proximity sensors defer possible runaway motion.
Within the spindle assemblies are mechanisms for adjustment of side to side and front to rear positioning, with dial indicators installed at the factory to aid in adjustment.
The diamond wheels mount to the air bearings on backing plates; the type of wheel installed gives the spindle its identity as either coarse or fine.
--[p101]-- The spindle drive system consists of a pulley system with a toothed belt drive connecting the lead screw to the reducer of the brushless DC servo motor. This arrangement converts motor drive into vertical linear motion, moving the spindle assembly up or down.
The ball screw assembly is attached to the spindle, and a counterbalance assembly mounted to the same spindle adjusts the amount of spindle weight seen by the wafer.
--[p101]-- COARSE/FINE SPINDLES
Identical except for the type of diamond wheel installed, the coarse and fine spindles grind the wafers on the left and right work chucks. Each is an air bearing spindle (for details, see below) mounted vertically and passing through a casting mounted to the vertical rails. The vertical rails are lubricated by the automatic lubricator; frictionless vertical movement is provided by the linear bearings.

===== [p160-160] MENUS USED IN BASIC OPERATION > NOTES: (1块) =====

Error Message - Until the servos have been homed, the 7AF will not respond to requests to run an auto grind cycle.
If you select the Grind menu without first homing, the screen will display an error message. Acknowledge the error message by touching OK; touch QUIT to return to the Main Menu to select the Home Machine menu.
Number of Minutes to Home - To home the machine takes five to six minutes.

===== [p464-488] PNEUMATIC ADJUSTMENTS > Notes: (3块) =====
--[p464]-- · Care should be taken to ensure that all air supply lines are thoroughly purged before connection to the spindles.
· Teflon tape must never be used on connections downstream of the filters.
· Nitrogen may be substituted for clean dry air.
--[p464]-- Notes:
· The air supplied must be clean and dry.
The air supply to the spindles should be filtered to remove oil and water particles in excess of one micron. Oil carryover at $2 1 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } \left( 3 9 . 8 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { F } \right)$ should not exceed .01 mg/cubic meter.
· The use of a freeze drier is recommended, with the pressure dew point not exceeding $7 . 2 \textrm { ^ o C } ( 4 5 \textrm { ^ o F } )$
--[p488]-- Notes:
For detailed information on the robot’s hardware, software, and programming, refer to the Equipe Technologies Atmospheric Robot, ATM - 100; Vacuum Robot, VAC - 100, Technical Manual, located in Appendix G, Manufacturer’s Documentation, of this (the Model 7AF Operation and Maintenance Manual) manual.

===== [p210-210] OPERATOR DAILY PREVENTIVEMAINTENANCE SCHEDULE > FAULT, ACKNOWLEDGED: RED STEADY, NO ALARM SOUNDS (2块) =====
--[p210]-- FAULT, ACKNOWLEDGED: RED STEADY, NO ALARM SOUNDS
This state indicates that a fault has occurred, but that an operator has touched the screen to acknowledge the presence of the fault. Clear this state by eliminating the cause of the fault. With this condition, wafer processing has stopped or will be stopped very soon.
--[p210]-- When this state exists, carefully observe the machine before stopping the cycle, as the machine will attempt to complete the processing of as many wafers as safely possible—wait for any wafers still being processed to finish before terminating the process.
(This page intentionally left blank)

===== [p421-421] MENUS USED IN MAINTENANCE AND CALIBRATION > Notes on Spindle Height and Probe Position Displays: (2块) =====
--[p421]-- The work chuck location is lost after homing (a) due to wheel wear if the machine has been processing wafers or (b) if the grind wheels or chucks have been dressed.
After referencing, the zero point is reestablished at the work chuck.
After power up and the initial referencing, for subsequent referencing, the count is upward from the work chuck beginning with zero.
Upward movement of the spindles is always positive; downward movement is always negative.
Note that negative numbers are always displayed in RED at the screen readout.
--[p421]-- Notes on Spindle Height and Probe Position Displays:
When the machine is first powered up, homing zeros out the screen readout for spindle height at the limit switch located at the top of the stroke.
During homing, the location of the top of the work chuck is determined by counting, beginning with zero, from the limit switch to the work chuck.

===== [p104-105] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > ROBOT (6块) =====
--[p105]-- The sealing of the body permits vacuum evacuation of the robot and its arm when a vacuum exhaust hose is attached to the flange on the bottom of the robot.
--[p105]-- In addition to the pulley system, the arm consists of two supporting rings, a limit ring, a virtual arm, a forearm, and an end effector base with dowel pins. The end effector base is part of the external timing pulley of the forearm.
The cover, made from a single piece of black anodized aluminum sheet metal and tightly closed on the robot's body with two plastic latches, protects the robot's mechanism and seals the robot's body.
--[p104]-- The robot automatically adjusts between 1/4-inch and 3/16-inch spaced cassettes without mechanical adjustments.
A closed loop servo driven three-axis mechanism (a ball screw with a system of nonexpanding short belts) provides movement. The robot consists of the following components: chassis, rotary unit, vertical displacement mechanism, arm, three DC motors with belt transmission system, and cover.
--[p104]-- The chassis is composed of two flanges, four steel supports, a mounting plate for the motor, the transmission for the theta axis, and an aluminum c-shaped channel to conduct cables and air hoses to the robot's arm.
The rotary unit gives support to the arm and provides angular displacement. It consists of the unit carrier with six adjustable cam follower bearings for the vertical displacement mechanism, a supporting plate, the vertical axis motor, a belt transmission gear, and the main bearing.
--[p104]-- The rotary unit is also equipped with a small aluminum reflective plate which, together with associated electronics, is used to generate the limit and home signals.
The vertical displacement assembly utilizes a 5-mm pitch lead screw, a vertical tube with four flat leading surfaces equally spaced around the tube, a lead screw support, and a top ring used to attach the robot arm.
The robot arm performs radial movements via a specially constructed belt driven pulley system.
--[p104]-- ROBOT
The Equipe Technologies robot performs wafer transportation, moving among the wafer cassette turrets, the pre-aligner, the work chucks, and the spin-rinse station. The robot is equipped with a rotating wrist and a single vacuum chuck end effector to permit picking the wafer up from either the bottom or top as needed. A wafer scanner mounted on the robot maps occupied and empty cassette slots and detects crossslotted wafers.

===== [p127-127] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > CLEAN DRY AIR SYSTEM (3块) =====
--[p127]-- CLEAN DRY AIR SYSTEM
Refer to the engineering drawings labeled 118168P\_ (pneumatic) and the Pneumatic Adjustments chapter of this manual for details on air use and related valve panels.
The inhouse clean dry air supply must be a minimum of 100 PSI for proper operation of all machine functions. The inhouse air supply enters from the rear of the machine through a ball valve, filter, regulator, and coalescing filter. These four parts are grouped together inline and located inside door 21.
--[p127]-- The 7AF has three sets of air filters, the main incoming air filter and two additional sets of filters in parallel for the air bearing spindles.
From the coalescing filter, the clean dry air supply is plumbed to a distribution manifold mounted at the bottom of the machine inside door 21. From the distribution manifold connection is made to a second manifold, located inside door 10, which serves the wafer handling section of the machine.
--[p127]-- All pneumatic lines are identified with banded identification tags at the termination points. These identification marks are encircled on the engineering drawings.

===== [p233-233] OPERATOR DAILY PREVENTIVEMAINTENANCE SCHEDULE > About Truing (1块) =====
--[p233]-- About Truing
On the Model 7AF the probes may be used to check the work chucks for true (radial runout, indicated by a probe fluctuation of less than one micron).
Truing a wheel or chuck prior to use ensures that the entire face of the wheel is in contact with the part at all times during the grinding cycle. The entire face thereby contributes to the grinding process, preventing excessive vibration or chattering.
Wheel truing removes runout, making the wheel surface parallel to that of the chuck.

===== [p40-68] MODEL 7AF > OVERVIEW (4块) =====
--[p40]-- OVERVIEW
The Model 7AF Wafer Grinder consists of two machine cabinet sections, grinding and wafer handling, bolted together at the right side of the machine and hinged at the left. The machine sections separate, and the handling section rolls away from the grinding section to provide internal access to both sections for adjustments and maintenance.
--[p68]-- The Control Panel section deals with the functions of items found on the control panel as well as additional "Emergency Off" buttons. The Control Computer section provides information on the monitor, the touch screen, the PC keyboard, and the menu displays.
--[p68]-- OVERVIEW
The chapter below provides an overview of the physical features, layout, and function of the Model 7AF Wafer Grinder. The illustrations presented are not to scale; their purpose is to offer a simplified view of the components of the machine.
The Cabinetry section details outside views of the machine, including doors and panels, location of standard emergency off buttons, and power switches. The Subassemblies section introduces the machine's key subassemblies.
--[p40]-- During the installation, leveling, and initial adjustment processes, the procedures for disconnecting and reconnecting the machine sections (and the internal utility connections) may need to be performed more than once.

===== [p462-462] PNEUMATIC ADJUSTMENTS > Assumption (1块) =====
--[p462]-- Assumption
The procedures below were written with the assumption that the reader is thoroughly familiar with the Model 7AF Wafer Grinder. If not, read the chapters in this manual on Physical Description, Installation, Mechanical Description, Control System Description, Power Distribution, Plumbing Description, and Operator Functions before beginning any procedure.

===== [p47-47] MODEL 7AF > LEVELING FEET (1块) =====
--[p47]-- LEVELING FEET
The grinding section of the machine has four leveling feet.
The leveling feet can be raised or lowered by turning the hex head adjustment bolt above each foot after loosening the locking nut.
Each leveling foot should be individually adjusted such that together they contact the floor with the machine's weight evenly distributed over all four feet.

===== [p60-60] MODEL 7AF > ELECTRICAL (3块) =====
--[p60]-- After making the electrical supply connection, leave the main power disconnect (main machine circuit breaker) in the "OFF" condition by moving the lever to its down position; close the electrical enclosure door and latch assembly tightly.
DO NOT attempt to turn on the main machine power switch until ALL machine utilities are connected.
--[p60]-- A hole must be drilled in the right side or top of the electrical enclosure in order to pass the wires through the cabinet wall to the circuit breaker. The location for this hole is left to the discretion of the customer. However, before drilling the hole, verify that there are no wires or components inside the enclosure that may interfere with the supply wire conduit.
In addition to connecting the three power wires, connect a safety ground wire to the back panel ground bus.
--[p60]-- ELECTRICAL
The electrical supply [I] is connected to the main machine circuit breaker (208 VAC), which in turn is connected to the main machine circuit breaker disconnect enclosure door handle assembly . The circuit breaker is mounted on the inside of the electrical disconnect box.
The door handle trips the lever of the disconnect enclosure door handle assembly to enable the circuit breaker.

===== [p61-61] MODEL 7AF > Notes: (1块) =====
--[p61]-- Notes:
The air supplied must be clean and dry.
The air supply to the spindle should be filtered to remove oil and water particles in excess of one micron. Oil carryover at 21 ° C (39.8 ° F) should not exceed .01 mg/cubic meter.
The use of a freeze drier is recommended, with the pressure dew point not exceeding 7.2 ° C (45 ° F).
Care should be taken to ensure that all air supply lines are thoroughly purged before connection to the spindles.
Teflon tape must never be used on connections downstream of the filters.
Nitrogen may be substituted for clean dry air.

===== [p451-451] ROBOT (AND PRE-ALIGNER) SETUP AND CALIBRATION > CAUTION! (2块) =====
--[p451]-- CAUTION!
Use the SAV command only after the robot wafer size has been set at 150 mm (6 inches) by issuing the "SWS 150" command.
To use SAV with the wafer size at any other setting will corrupt all coordinates for all the stations.
The "RSA" command must also be issued before using the "SAV" command.
Follow the three-step sequence shown below when using the SAV command:
1. RSA   
2. SWS 150   
3. SAV
--[p451]-- Saves all robot coordinates, variables, and parameters to the control computer's nonvolatile memory. This command must be used when coordinates, variables, or parameters are updated or changed. If the "SAV" command is not used, the new data will be lost if power is turned off to the controller.

--[p121]-- For those doors equipped with double-acting spring loaded switches (see the table below): when the service door is in place, the switch plunger is depressed and the contact is closed. When the door is out of position, the switch contact is open. ===== [p100-100] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > BRIDGE ASSEMBLY (3块) =====
--[p100]-- Encoder feedback constantly reports back to the control computer the exact position and velocity of the bridge assembly.
The bridge is two separate pieces tied together by a stress-proof shaft to eliminate the possibility of transferring vibration from one spindle to the other.
--[p100]-- Two pulleys and a toothed drive belt connect the lead screw to a brushless DC servo motor. This arrangement converts motor drive force into linear motion, moving the bridge assembly left or right. The motor, mounted to the bed in the right side rear of the machine, is accessible through doors 16 and 17. Limit switches and shock absorber hard stops at each end of the rails ensure the bridge assembly does not "run away", crashing into the side walls of the machine.
--[p100]-- BRIDGE ASSEMBLY
The bridge assembly encloses and supports the left and right upper spindle assemblies and their associated hardware. Supported by two rails mounted on a solid framework, the bridge assembly moves between the left and right work chucks.
Eight (four per spindle) linear bearing blocks, attached to the underside of the bridge assembly, ride along the top of the rails. The drive assembly is a recirculating ball and lead screw supported by the machine's framework at each end.

===== [p27-27] ABOUT THIS MANUAL > ABOUT THE MACHINE (3块) =====
--[p27]-- To achieve these goals Strasbaugh engineers have incorporated a number of enhancements over previous grinders built by Strasbaugh and by its competitors. Design emphasis has focused on maximizing potential grinding results, versatility, reliability, and simplicity of operation.
The 7AF is built of special materials with optimum flatness and stable thermal characteristics.
--[p27]-- In addition to superior mechanical design, the grinder utilizes efficient, reliable computer and coprocessor systems for machine and process control functions. The combined benefits of ergonomic design and state-of-the-art mechanical tolerances and machine controls provide the superior process yield potential inherent in the Model 7AF Wafer Grinder.
--[p27]-- ABOUT THE MACHINE
The nTellect (Model 7AF) Wafer Grinder is designed specifically for mechanical grinding to remove material from the back side (the side opposite the electronics) of semiconductor wafers to the desired thickness. The in- process digital measurement probe is in contact with the wafer throughout the grinding process, providing constant feedback and permitting grinding to an accuracy in microns. Fully automated wafer handling provides cassette to cassette processing.

===== [p186-186] TRUING AND DRESSING THE GRIND WHEELS AND WORK CHUCKS > About Truing (1块) =====
--[p186]-- About Truing
On the Model 7AF the probes may be used to check the work chucks for true (radial runout, indicated by a probe fluctuation of less than one micron).
Truing a wheel or chuck prior to use ensures that the entire face of the wheel is in contact with the part at all times during the grinding cycle. The entire face thereby contributes to the grinding process, preventing excessive vibration or chattering.
Wheel truing removes runout, making the wheel surface parallel to that of the chuck.

===== [p103-103] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > LEFT/RIGHT CONDITIONING ARMS (3块) =====
--[p103]-- LEFT/RIGHT CONDITIONING ARMS
Each conditioning arm stone assembly consists of a circular rotating stone brush which applies down force on the ceramic work chuck, cleaning the chuck between grindings. To prevent damage to the chuck, the force applied is equal only to the weight of the stone assembly. An air motor rotates the stone brush, and at the end of the conditioning cycle the arm parks itself off to the side within the grinding pan.
--[p103]-- • A secondary cylinder lowers the arm, moving it down over the work chuck to the required height for conditioning.
• An air motor rotates the stone brush.
--[p103]-- Switches on the assembly indicate whether the brush is parked or engaged.
The following is the conditioning arm sequence of movements:
A pneumatic cylinder moves the arm assembly shaft up, causing the entire assembly to move the conditioning stone brush from park height to the required height for moving to engage position.
• A rotary actuator moves the arm to engage position (a sensor indicates position).

===== [p71-71] MODEL 7AF > Effects of Opening Doors (2块) =====
--[p71]-- Effects of Opening Doors
Opening door 10, 17, 18, or 20 at any time shuts power down to the entire machine, including the control computer. Recover by manually clearing any leftover wafers, powering up and rehoming the machine.
Opening door 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, or 19 during an auto grind cycle terminates the cycle and inhibits the servos. Recover by manually clearing any leftover wafers and restarting the auto cycle.
Opening door 7, 8, or 9 has no effect on machine power or the cycle running.
--[p71]-- Opening door 5 or 6 halts the cycle; closing doors 5 and 6 resumes the cycle. (Their function is similar to that of the Pause Cycle button on the Grind Cycle menu.)

===== [p30-30] ABOUT THIS MANUAL > GENERAL OPERATION (2块) =====
--[p30]-- Disconnect the power when servicing or repairing the machine.
DO NOT operate the machine without proper electrical grounding.
DO NOT wear loose clothing that could be caught by machine parts in motion.
• Wear SAFETY GLASSES whenever working near moving machinery.
--[p30]-- GENERAL OPERATION
Operating the machine with loose wafers inside is harmful to the machine and wafers. Always remove loose wafers and obstructions before beginning machine operation.
DO NOT at any time attempt to put hands or objects beyond the Operator Doors while the machine is in motion.
Keep all guards and covers in place and in good repair.
DO NOT attempt to bypass safety interlocks.
Keep all control and electrical cabinet doors closed and latched.

===== [p449-449] ROBOT (AND PRE-ALIGNER) SETUP AND CALIBRATION > [Z-AXIS] (2块) =====
--[p449]-- [Z-AXIS]
Used to move the robot or any individual axis a specified distance from its current position. The command "MOVR R,1000" would move the robot arm one inch from its current position. However, the command "MOVR 1000,1000,1000" would move all three axes 1000 increments from their current position.
--[p449]-- [Z-AXIS]
Used to move the robot or any individual axis to an absolute position. The command "MOVA Z,4000" would move the Z-axis to position 4000. However, the command "MOVA 1200,-8400,300" would move the robot to the absolute position of (1200,- 8400,300).

===== [p209-209] OPERATOR DAILY PREVENTIVEMAINTENANCE SCHEDULE > FAULT: RED FLASHING, ALARM SOUNDS (3块) =====
--[p209]-- · detectable error by the operator (example: failure to place a receive cassette in the machine)
· dangerous condition (example: loss of air pressure)
· temporary but potentially serious condition (example: robot vacuum error)
Operation under dangerous conditions will be stopped to the best of the machine’s ability, but any wafer processing that can continue safely will proceed.
This state will be cleared when the reason for the fault is cleared.
--[p209]-- FAULT: RED FLASHING, ALARM SOUNDS
Whenever a "FAULT" message is displayed, requesting operator attention, the light tower changes to flashing read and the alarm sounds within five seconds of the screen’s display of the message. The five second delay before the light begins flashing and the alarm begins sounding permits the operator to respond before the alarm sounds. A fault state will occur when wafer processing is stopped due to any of the following
--[p209]-- If the fault is spontaneously cleared and production is continued, the previous state will be restored. If the fault persists, the operator can acknowledge the fault by touching any button or any inactive part of the menu screen to communicate to the machine that the fault has been recognized. After the operator acknowledges the fault, the machine will move to a "Fault Acknowledged" state (see below) with the "FAULT" message continuing to display but the alarm off.

===== [p29-29] ABOUT THIS MANUAL > ELECTRICAL DISTRIBUTION AND CONTROL (5块) =====
--[p29]-- A high resolution color monitor with touch screen interfaces the grinder with the user through menu-oriented commands displayed on the monitor.
The 7AF uses a standard "off the shelf" computer package rather than a customized card cage package to maintain simplicity, reliability, and economy.
--[p29]-- The axes controlled through slot 3 are work chuck left and right, Z travel of the coarse and fine grind spindles, side to side motion of the bridge, the spin-rinse station, and rotation of the two grind spindles. Motors and controllers for each of the eight axes (all grinding and bridge motions and the spin-rinse station) are located at the lower right side of the machine. The two inverters for the two upper spindles reside in the inverter enclosure at the rear of the machine.
--[p29]-- Controllers for the robot and pre-aligner are located at the lower left side of the machine.
The control computer, robot and pre-aligner controllers, input/output, servo motor controllers, digital measurement probes, and the robot/pre-aligner teach terminal maintain communication for complete control of all machine functions. Note that with further development of the control software, the teach terminal will be eliminated.
--[p29]-- ELECTRICAL DISTRIBUTION AND CONTROL
The Model 7AF Wafer Grinder’s electrical distribution and control systems are designed to provide all necessary control functions for polish process optimization while maintaining the reliability and ease of use necessary for the production environment.
The heart of the control system is the control computer, an industrial personal computer (PC), providing maximum reliability and functionality in an industry standard package.
--[p29]-- In addition to the control computer and interface hardware, the control system includes in situ measurement of thickness control (via a card residing in slot 1 of the control computer), an industry standard input/output (I/O) system (card in slot 2), and dedicated control of eight of the grinder's servo motor axes, (card in slot 3).

Homing A "homing" message displayed above a machine component icon indicates the component is currently being homed.
Homed A "homed" message displayed above a machine component icon indicates the component has been homed.
REFD A "REFD" message displayed above the coarse or fine spindle icon indicates the spindle has been referenced.
Error Messages Error messages indicating faults that prevent homing are displayed when appropriate.
For detailed information on error messages, refer to the Troubleshooting chapter of this manual.

===== [p102-102] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > AIR BEARING SPINDLES (3块) =====
--[p102]-- AIR BEARING SPINDLES
The four Westwind (Federal Mogul) air bearing spindles use clean dry air flowing through close tolerance rotating surfaces to provide smooth, stiff rotational motion. (A circular disk on a shaft hovers within a stabilizing plate which rides on air.) The absence of metal to metal contact provides a high degree of stiffness and eliminates friction, resulting in cooler operating temperatures and longer spinning.
--[p102]-- Due to the close tolerances involved, the air used must be clean and dry to prevent clogging of the air ports. For proper function of the spindles, consistent maintenance of the air system must be performed.
The grind (upper) spindles each require 5.5 cubic feet per minute (CFM) at 70 PSI clean dry air. The work (lower) spindles each require 3.3 CFM at 80 PSI. A pair of air filters provides the required filtration and isolation for the air supply for each spindle.
--[p102]-- A gauge on the outlet of each filter pair indicates the supply pressure at each spindle (assuming negligible pressure drop in the supply tubing).
If filter elements accumulate excessive contamination, resulting in insufficient supply pressure, the filter elements should be replaced. Pressure switches are connected to each spindle supply to provide added protection against spindle failure. Each switch is adjusted to open when pressure falls below the minimum requirement.
However, it is still advisable to implement filter inspection and replacement as a part of the preventive maintenance schedule.

===== [p223-223] OPERATOR DAILY PREVENTIVEMAINTENANCE SCHEDULE > WAFER PARAMETERS (2块) =====
--[p223 [表]]-- WAFER PARAMETERS
WARNING! If the Wafer Diameter is not correct, the robot will crash into the wafers.
Be sure to set the Wafer Diameter (located in the Wafer Parameters box) to match the diameter of the wafers to be polished.
The three wafer parameters, listed below, are consistent for both coarse and fine grind.   
One set of wafer parameters is stored per recipe.
Feed WaferThickness | value entered = the maximum wafer thickness (in microns)when measured before grinding.
--[p223]-- TapeThickness | value entered = the thickness (in microns) of the protectivetape used on the front side of the wafer. This value is anoffset for wafer thickness.
WaferDiameter | value entered = the diameter (in inches or millimeters) of thewafer to be ground.

===== [p459-459] ROBOT (AND PRE-ALIGNER) SETUP AND CALIBRATION > MACHINES WITH HOME INDEX HARDWARE INSTALLED (2块) =====
--[p459]-- Referring to the Machine (Calibration) Setup Entry Menu section of this chapter, change the offset in fractions of a rotation, positive or negative:
· Use positive numbers to rotate the offset counterclockwise.
· Use negative numbers to rotate the offset clockwise.
Use the Machine Variables LT Chuck Home Offset (variable 10) and RT Chuck Home Offset (variable 11) for the left and right chucks, respectively.
Note: The spin chuck does not have an offset.
--[p459]-- MACHINES WITH HOME INDEX HARDWARE INSTALLED
During installation, the PC-DSP card must be loaded with the configuration that supports this function. In addition, jumpers must be installed on the PC-DSP card grounding the home input signals from the work and spin chucks.
With the hardware installed and chuck homing initiated, the homing procedure will first locate the edge of the index pulse. After the edge is located, the chuck will rotate to an optional offset.

===== [p233-233] OPERATOR DAILY PREVENTIVEMAINTENANCE SCHEDULE > About Dressing (1块) =====
--[p233]-- About Dressing
Dressing a wheel improves or alters its cutting action. The dressing action removes the outside layer of dulled diamonds and any loading of material that the wheel may have picked up, exposing the sharp, strong diamonds.
Dressing a chuck conditions its surface to remove debris and unclog vacuum pores, resulting in reduced thickness variations within the wafers processed.

===== [p119-119] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > DC DISTRIBUTION (2块) =====
--[p119]-- DC DISTRIBUTION
The DC voltage distribution consists of three individual power supplies, 1PS for 24 VDC, 2PS for +/- 15 VDC, and 3PS for 5 VDC, and their respective terminal blocks, TS24 , TS23, and TS22. Each DC power supply has its terminal strip to branch out DC power throughout the machine as shown in the electrical schematics.
Power supply 1PS sources 24 VDC power for inputs and outputs on the digital I/O racks 1MR, 2MR, 3MR, and 4MR.
--[p119]-- These outputs enable two variable frequency AC drives and the six brushless servo controllers as well as the solenoid valves for the pneumatic, vacuum, and water lines. Power supply 2PS sources +/- 15 VDC power for all the analog inputs and outputs found on the analog I/O racks. Power supply 3PS provides +5 VDC to the digital I/O racks 1MR, 2MR, 3MR, and 4MR, the two analog I/O racks, and the servo controller I/O to power their internal circuitry.

===== [p186-186] TRUING AND DRESSING THE GRIND WHEELS AND WORK CHUCKS > About Dressing (1块) =====
--[p186]-- About Dressing
Dressing a wheel improves or alters its cutting action. The dressing action removes the outside layer of dulled diamonds and any loading of material that the wheel may have picked up, exposing the sharp, strong diamonds.
Dressing a chuck conditions its surface to remove debris and unclog vacuum pores, resulting in reduced thickness variations within the wafers processed.

===== [p110-111] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > SERVO CONTROL (3块) =====
--[p110 [表]]-- SERVO CONTROL
The machine has six brushless DC servo motors powered by brushless DC servo amplifiers and control boards. Two AC servo motors are powered by a pulse width modulated variable frequency drive. Velocity, position, and direction are controlled by the motion control board located in the control computer.
The servo motors are labeled axis 1 through 8. The table below shows the motion provided by each:
Axis Label | Motion Provided
1 | bridge side to side motion
--[p111]-- The instructions are received by the servo controller card through a communications bus on the motherboard. Each of the servo channels interprets the computer's digital instructions and outputs an analog velocity command signal to the eight motors' amplifier modules. All eight axes use optical encoder feedback. This system forms a complete closed loop servo motion control system.
--[p111]-- 2 | coarse grind wheel up/down
3 | fine grind wheel up/down
4 | coarse grind spindle rotation
5 | fine grind spindle rotation
6 | left work chuck rotation
7 | right work chuck rotation
8 | spin rinse chuck rotation
Each motor is individually programmed for velocity, acceleration, and position. Instructions for motion of each servo motor originate from the main program of the control computer.

===== [p81-81] MODEL 7AF > GRINDING AREA (2块) =====
--[p81]-- To prevent wafer breakage from grinding debris, conditioning is done just before a new wafer is placed on the chuck.
The Left (8) and Right (9) Work Chucks hold and rotate the wafers; wafers are retained by vacuum.
--[p81]-- GRINDING AREA
The Bridge Assembly (1) moves the upper Coarse (2) and Fine (3) spindles left and right over the work chucks.
The Coarse (2) and Fine (3) Spindles grind the wafers on the left and right work chucks.
The Left (4) and Right (5) Digital Measurement Probes provide stationary in-process measuring of wafer thickness.
The Left (6) and Right (7) Conditioning Arms are equipped with cleaning material to remove debris from the chucks between wafer grinding.

--[p264]-- The initial alignments section provides detailed procedures for grinding area and handling area adjustments to be performed when the machine is moved and at other times as needed.

===== [p62-62] MODEL 7AF > DE-IONIZED WATER (1块) =====
--[p62]-- DE-IONIZED WATER
De-Ionized water is used as coolant during grinding and as a wafer rinse at the spinrinse station. The DI water system is equipped with a temperature gauge. If temperature-controlled DI water is desired, it must be supplied, conditioned in advance of entering the machine.
The connections for DI water in [C] and DI water out [D] are 1/2-inch FNPT located at the lower rear of the machine.
A bulkhead fitting is provided to connect the system to facility plumbing.
The plumbing should be selected to provide the necessary flow and pressure for the machine.

===== [p384-384] CHANGING THE GRIND WHEELS > GOAL: Tighten the six socket head bolts to 8 foot-pounds (96 inchpounds). (1块) =====
--[p384]-- GOAL: Tighten the six socket head bolts to 8 foot-pounds (96 inchpounds).
a. Tighten one bolt to 8 foot-pounds.
b. Manually rotate the grind wheel 180 ° to expose a bolt on the opposite side of the grind wheel..
c. Tighten the bolt opposite the one tightened in Step 6.a to 8 foot-pounds.
d. Repeat Steps a. through c. until all 6 bolts have been tightened to 8 footpounds (96 inch-pounds).
7. Repeat Steps 6.a through 6.d, immediately above, tightening each bolt to 10 foot-pounds (120 inch-pounds).

===== [p149-149] MENUS USED IN BASIC OPERATION > About Dressing (1块) =====
--[p149]-- About Dressing
Dressing a wheel improves or alters its cutting action. The dressing action removes the outside layer of dulled diamonds and any loading of material that the wheel may have picked up, exposing the sharp, strong diamonds.
Dressing a chuck conditions its surface to remove debris and unclog vacuum pores, resulting in reduced thickness variations within the wafers processed.

===== [p63-63] MODEL 7AF > INDUSTRIAL WASTE (1块) =====
--[p63]-- INDUSTRIAL WASTE
The industrial waste drain [A], the machine’s main drain, is connected via a twoinch pipe a the lower rear of the machine.
The industrial waste drain carries DI water and residual amounts of product removal residue; thus, it may not require any special handling provisions.
An external cleanout is recommended for the drain pipe. A pipe union is also recommended--located near the drain pipe connection to facilitate future pipe servicing or possible machine moving.

===== [p447-447] ROBOT (AND PRE-ALIGNER) SETUP AND CALIBRATION > ROBOT COORDINATES (1块) =====
--[p447]-- ROBOT COORDINATES
The position information for the robot is represented in the form of polar coordinates. The polar coordinates are rotational (Theta or T), radial extension (Radius or R), and height (Z-axis or Z). Therefore, a specific position would be represented in the form, (T, R, Z). The user can identify a specific set of coordinates by assigning them a station name. Valid names are A-Z and a-z.
For example, station "B" can be assigned the coordinates (100,500,500) and station "b" can be assigned coordinates (2000,400,1500).

===== [p355-355] MECHANICAL MAINTENANCE > 4. Correct the height: (1块) =====
--[p355]-- 4. Correct the height:
a. Loosen the three clamp screws of the locking collar by rotating them counterclockwise.
b. Lotate the large adjusting screw centered on the locking collar clockwise or counterclockwise as needed to meet the goal.
Note: The adjusting screw is hollow to accommodate the sensor wires.
c. When the goal is met, rotate the clamp screws clockwise, tightening them to 50%.
Note: When the clamp screws are sufficiently tightened, the platform support will not wobble on the rotary actuator shaft.

===== [p441-441] SECS / GEM Interface > 3.2.3 SECS-I Blocks Received (1块) =====
--[p441]-- 3.2.3 SECS-I Blocks Received
Blocks received by the Equipment should be formatted as described above (except with the R-bit set to "0"), although the rules are more relaxed:
1. If a message consists of a single block, the Block Number may be zero (0x0000) or one (0x0001).
2. The Equipment is indifferent to the R-bit setting.

===== [p446-447] SECS / GEM Interface > 3.9 State Diagrams (5块) =====
--[p446]-- 3.9 State Diagrams
This document uses several Finite State Machine diagrams to describe the current condition of the Equipment's SECS link, material handling mechanisms, and process cycle. Each Finite State Machine diagram includes a State Diagram and a complete description of the states and state transitions.
All Finite State Diagrams have been prepared in the format specified in the GEM standard.
--[p446]-- The entity described by the diagrams will be in one and only one of the sub-states at all times.
4. Variables representing the current state of an entity do not contain values for super-states, only the lowest substate is represented.
5. State transitions are represented by single-headed arrows.
6. Each state transition is a Collection Event, and it has a unique Collection Event ID (CEID)
7.
--[p447]-- An arrow directly into a super-state to the C (conditional) symbol describes a transition to a particular sub-state based on some other relevant data. The conditional data is not represented in the diagram but is described in the associated text.
--[p446]-- This notation is required as a fundamental part of GEM compliance and must be included in the Equipment SECS Interface Documentation. This notation is the "Statechart" notation developed by David Harel.
The following are the major characteristics of this notation as it is used in this document:
1. Each state is represented by a rectangle with rounded corners.
2. A collection of sub-states may be grouped into a super-state.
3.
--[p446]-- An arrow directly from a super-state to another state describes a Collection Event that can occur while the entity is in any one of the sub-states contained in the super-state.
8. An arrow directly into a super-state to the H\* (history) symbol describes a transition to the lowest sub-state which described the entity just before the transition out of the super-state.
9.

===== [p466-466] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.4.4 Setting Equipment Constants (1块) =====
--[p466]-- 5.4.4 Setting Equipment Constants
The Equipment Operator can change the value for Equipment Constants. Once the Operator has changed an EC value, the Equipment will note the EqConstChange Event (CEID 7). The VID for the changed EC will be reported to the Host in the variable ECIDCHANGE (VID 258).

===== [p444-444] SECS / GEM Interface > 3.6 SEMI E10 Standard (1块) =====
--[p444]-- 3.6 SEMI E10 Standard
The SEMI E10 Standard is another document published by SEMI. It provides a guideline for definition and measurement of equipment reliability, availability, and maintainability (RAM). This document defines six basic Equipment States which define how equipment time is categorized.
The SECS Interface on the 7AF will allow the Host to determine the current E10 state. These Equipment States are as defined in the following version of the standard:
1.
E10-1992 (Section 3, Equipment States)

===== [p497-497] SECS / GEM Interface > 6.20 S2F16 - Equipment Constant Send Acknowledge (1块) =====
--[p497 [表]]-- 6.20 S2F16 - Equipment Constant Send Acknowledge
Normal completion returns a zero (0) in EAC. If any ECID or ECV in S2F15 is invalid, then EAC contains a non-zero value, and the Equipment rejects the entire S2F15. Possible EAC values are:
EAC | Description
0x00 | OK
0x01 | At least one ECID invalid
0x02 | Busy, Denied
0x03 | At least one ECV out of range

===== [p400-400] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK > Introduction (5块) =====
--[p400]-- The lockout device must be substantial enough to prevent removal without use of excessive force or unusual techniques.
Tagout is the placement of a tagout device (a tag or other prominent warning device and a means of attachment) on an energy isolation device to indicate that the energy isolating device and the equipment being controlled may not be operated until the tagout device is removed.
--[p400]-- Introduction
On October 30, 1989, the Lockout/Tagout Standard, 29 CFR 1910.147, went into effect. It was created to help reduce the death and injury rate caused by the unexpected energization or startup of machines, or the release of stored energy. The standard covers servicing and maintenance of machines and equipment in which unexpected energization, start-up or release of stored energy could cause injury [29 CFR 1910.147 (a)(1)(i), 1910.147 (a)(2)(I)].
--[p400]-- The lockout device shall be used unless the employer can demonstrate that the utilization of a tagout system will provide full employee protection. The tagout device shall be non-reusable, attached by hand, self-locking, and non-releasing with a minimum unlocking strength of no less than 50 pounds and must be at least equivalent to an allenvironment tolerant nylon cable tie.
--[p400]-- Lockout is the placement of a lockout device on an energy isolation device (circuit breaker, slide gate, line valve, disconnect switch, etc.) to ensure that the energy isolating device and equipment being controlled cannot be operated until the lockout device is removed. A lockout device uses a positive means such as a lock (key or combination type) to hold an energy-isolating device in a safe position and prevent the energization of a machine or equipment.
--[p400]-- Normal production operations, cords and plugs under exclusive control, and hot tap operations are not covered [29 CPR 1910.147 (a)(2)(ii)]. This is intended to apply to energy sources such as electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, chemical, nuclear and thermal.
