===== [p467-467] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.4.5 Event Reports (2块) =====
--[p467]-- 5.4.5 Event Reports
The 7AF has a fixed set of Events which can occur. Each Event is identified by a unique Collection Event ID (CEID).   
The CEIDs which exist are shown in "Appendix B -- Collection Events".
When an Event occurs, the Equipment sends the appropriate S6F11 Event Report message to the Host (if that particular event has been enabled). Event Reports are defined by the Host (S2F33) and linked to a specific CEID (S2F35).
--[p467]-- The Equipment allows the Host to enable and disable Event Reports using S2F37. If the Host enables a CEID, for which no Event Report is defined, the Equipment will send a "null" (no data) report when the event occurs.
The Host can "force" Event Reports on the Equipment using the following Event Report Request messages:
S6F15 Host Requests an Event Report associated with a CEID.
S6F17 Host requests an Annotated Event Report associated with a CEID.
S6F19 Host requests an Event Report associated with a Report ID.
S6F21 Host requests an Annotated Event Report associated with a Report ID.

===== [p470-470] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.6.2 Host Management of Process Programs (3块) =====
--[p470]-- The Host can delete one or more Process Programs from the 7AF library by using S7F17 (Process Program Delete).
The Host can determine which Process Programs are currently stored in the 7AF library by using S7F19 (Process Program Directory).
--[p470]-- 5.6.2 Host Management of Process Programs
Process Programs are saved to disk on the equipment. Process Programs are typically created and updated at the 7AF. However, the 7AF provides complete facilities for the Host to manage the storage and use of Process Programs. This allows the 7AF to operate cooperatively with Host-implemented systems. The Host has the following capabilities:
The Host can upload a Process Program from the 7AF Library by using S7F5 (Process Program Request).
--[p470]-- The equipment operator can also initiate a Process Program Upload through the 7AF's user interface.
The Host can download a Process Program to the 7AF library by using S7F3 (Process Program Send). The Host may send S7F1 (Multi-block Inquire) to the equipment before sending a multi-block Process Program. The equipment operator can also initiate a Process Program Download through the 7AF's user interface.

===== [p465-465] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.3.4.5 Edit Screens (VID 15 = 6) (1块) =====
--[p465]-- 5.3.4.5 Edit Screens (VID 15 = 6)
This state means that the Equipment is being used to examine and possibly change recipe parameters.

===== [p494-494] SECS / GEM Interface > 6.12 S1F16 - Off-Line Acknowledge (1块) =====
--[p494]-- 6.12 S1F16 - Off-Line Acknowledge
Equipment Control State transits to Host Off-Line and sends this message in response to S1F15 primary. OFLACK is always zero.

===== [p440-440] SECS / GEM Interface > 3.2.2 SECS-I Blocks Transmitted (1块) =====
--[p440]-- 3.2.2 SECS-I Blocks Transmitted
The Equipment uses the following SECS-I conventions in the blocks it sends:
1. The Device ID is present in every block, with the R-bit always set to "1".
2. The Block Number is always one (0x0001) for the first block of a message.
3. For Primary messages, the System Bytes are generated unique for each message. For Secondary messages, the System Bytes are replicated from the received Primary message.

===== [p480-480] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.12.2 Spooling Sequence (1块) =====
--[p480]-- 5.12.2 Spooling Sequence
Messages are sent to the spool only if the Host has enabled these messages for spooling. This precondition will not be repeated throughout this section. Assume that the messages referred to in this section have been enabled for spooling.
While spooling is active, the Host may initiate primary messages and the 7AF will respond, if it is in the COMMUNICATING state.

<L> \* Instead of L [3]

===== [p453-453] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.1.1.2.2.2 NOT COMMUNICATING (3块) =====
--[p453]-- 5.1.1.2.2.2 NOT COMMUNICATING
The SECS link to the Host is enabled at the 7AF, and the Equipment is attempting to determine if the link is active. The Equipment periodically sends S1F13 (Establish Communications Request).
If the connect is not successful for any reason, the Equipment will try again periodically forever. The time between attempts is controlled by the Equipment Constant ESTABLISHCOMMUNICATIONSTIMER.
--[p453]-- In ENABLED state, the 7AF will accept messages from the Host, but will ignore any messages except S1F13 and S1F14. The 7AF will respond to the S1F13 while the Communication State is ENABLED or COMMUNICATING, but it will not send S1F13 once communications have been established.
--[p453]-- This variable (VID 52) can range from 0 to 32000 seconds, with default of 60 seconds.
Once the Host has responded with S1F14 (Establish Communications Acknowledge), the Communication State will change to COMMUNICATING.
The Host can also attempt to establish communications by sending S1F13. The Equipment will accept the message and respond with S1F14 and the Communication State will change to COMMUNICATING.

===== [p471-471] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.7 Remote Commands (4块) =====
--[p471]-- 5.7 Remote Commands
Setup and processing at the 7AF can be guided by either a local operator or by a Host computer. This section describes the remote commands available to the Host.
Much of the behavior of the 7AF and its acceptance of remote commands is directed by requirements of the Control State.   
For a complete description of the Control State, please see section 5.2, "Control States".
The 7AF will accept remote commands only when the Control State is Remote.
--[p471]-- While in the Local state, the Host can not put the Equipment into Remote, this must be done by an operator at the Equipment.
The Host has the ability to configure whether the Equipment will transition to Remote or local as a default upon entering the On-Line state from Off-Line. This is done by setting The ONLINESUBSTATE Equipment Constant (VID 44) to 4 (Local) or 5 (Remote).
--[p471]-- Once in the Remote state, the Host has the authority to issue any of these remote commands and they will not be rejected because of an invalid control state. Commands may be rejected for other reasons (trying to start a process with no material loaded, etc.).
While in Remote state, the Operator still has the ability to issue commands and change the control state. If the operator issues a command while in Remote state, the 7AF will send the OperatorCommand collection event if enabled (CEID 11).
--[p471]-- When the Operator "grabs" control away from the Host by changing the Control State to not Remote, the 7AF will send either the CONTROLSTATELOCAL (CEID 13) or EQUIPMENTOFFLINE (CEID 5002) event to the Host. The Host also has the ability to put the Equipment into a Local state by sending the LOCAL remote command while in Remote state.

===== [p398-398] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK > Sequence of Lockout Procedure (3块) =====
--[p398]-- Sequence of Lockout Procedure
1. Notify all affected employees that a lockout is required and the reason therefore.
2. If the equipment is operating, shut it down by the normal stopping procedure (depress stop button, open toggle switch, etc.).
3. For each energy source, operate the switch, valve, or other energy isolating device so that the energy source(s) (electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, etc.) is disconnected or isolated from the equipment.
--[p398]-- Stored energy, such as that in capacitors, springs, elevated machine members, rotating flywheels, hydraulic systems, and air, gas, steam, or water pressure, etc., must also be dissipated or restrained by methods such as grounding, repositioning, blocking, bleeding-down, etc.
4. Lockout the energy isolating devices with an assigned individual lock.
5.
--[p398]-- After ensuring that no personnel are exposed and as a check on having disconnected the energy sources, operate the push button or other normal operating controls to make certain the equipment will not operate.
CAUTION: Return operating controls to neutral position after the test.
6. The equipment is now locked out.

===== [p497-498] SECS / GEM Interface > 6.22 S2F18 - Date and Time Data (2块) =====
--[p497]-- 6.22 S2F18 - Date and Time Data
S2F18 \* H<->E <A TIME> . \* TIME – Date and Time
This message contains the current Date and Time, specified in either a 12-byte or 16-byte format. The 16-byte format was defined to support Y2K compatibility, and is supported when the TIMEFORMAT variable (VID 141) is set to “1”. To maintain compatibility with older systems, the 12-byte format is supported when the TIMEFORMAT variable is set to “0”.
If TIMEFORMAT = 0, the format is YYMMDDhhmmss
--[p498 [表]]-- If TIMEFORMAT = 1, the format is YYYYMMDDhhmmsscc
YYYY | Year, 0000 to 9999
MM | Month, 01 to 12
DD | Day, 01 to 31
hh | Hours, 00 to 23
mm | Minutes, 00 to 59
SS | Seconds, 00 to 59
cc | Centiseconds
When the Equipment receives a good S2F18, it sets its internal clock/calendar. When receiving S2F18, the Equipment will discard an invalid date or time. For example, if the date is good but the time is bad, the Equipment sets its date but not its time.

===== [p498-498] SECS / GEM Interface > 6.23 S2F21 - Remote Command (1块) =====
--[p498]-- 6.23 S2F21 - Remote Command
S2F21 [W] \* H->E <A RCMD> . \* Remote command string
Note: This message is only provided for compatibility with non-GEM Hosts.
The Host sends a Remote Command to the Equipment.
The 7AF ignores case when performing validity checks on the RCMD strings.
The Host may optionally set the W-Bit to "1" in S2F21. If so, the Equipment replies with S2F22.

===== [p457-457] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.2.1.2.5 On-Line/REMOTE (1块) =====
--[p457]-- 5.2.1.2.5 On-Line/REMOTE
The remote Host Computer has control of the 7AF using S2F41 (Remote Command). For details see section 5.7 "Remote Commands".
The Operator may issue the ABORT commands while in Remote. These commands will generate an OperatorCommand event (CEID 11) as well as other messages attached to these activities.

===== [p457-457] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.2.1.2.2 Off-Line/HOST OFF-LINE (2块) =====
--[p457]-- 5.2.1.2.2 Off-Line/HOST OFF-LINE
While in this state, the 7AF will accept either the S1F17 (Go Online), or the S1F13 (Connect Request) message. When in this state, the operator has allowed the Host to put the Equipment On-Line, but the Host has not yet done so, or the Host has just put the Equipment Off-Line by sending S1F15. The Host may request for the Equipment to come On-Line by sending the S1F17 Go Online message. The Operator can not put the Equipment On-Line from this state.
--[p457]-- The S1F13/S1F14 messages are used to maintain the Communications Finite State Machine. All messages (except S1F13 and S1F17) received will be replied to with the SnF0 ABORT message. The Equipment will not send any primary messages except for S1F13 when necessary to establish communications, and the S9F1 and S9F9 messages for SECS errors.

===== [p468-468] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.5.3 Enable/Disable (2块) =====
--[p468]-- 5.5.3 Enable/Disable
The Host can use S5F3 (Enable/Disable Alarms) to control which alarms the 7AF should report. Using S5F3, the Host can specify for each ALID whether the Equipment should report that alarm when it occurs. When an alarm transition occurs, if that ALID is enabled the Equipment will send an alarm report message to the Host. If the ALID is disabled, the Equipment will not send the alarm message.
--[p468]-- The Host can use S2F37 to enable or disable the CEIDs associated with these alarm transitions.
The 7AF saves Alarm Enable/Disable settings on a disk file. When the Equipment powers up, it will restore Alarm Enable/Disable settings to the same condition they had at power off.

--[p445]-- · For a non-GEM Host, build appropriate Report Definitions, Links, and Enables (S2F33, S2F35, S2F37) so that S6F9 or S6F3 event reports contain the desired data. See "How to Configure", below.

--[p445]-- 3.7.2 GEM Configuration
This Equipment is configurable for operation with most older Host Computers which do not support the GEM message set, or support an older version of GEM.
· Equipment Constant "CONFIGALARMS" (VID 46) selects the message the Equipment will send for Alarm Reports. "ConfigAlarms" may be 0, 1, or 2, selection S5F1, S5F71, or S5F73, respectively.
· Equipment Constant "CONFIGCONNECT" (VID 236) selects the message the Equipment will send for Connect Request.
--[p445]-- "ConfigConnect" may be 0, 1, or 2, selecting S1F1, S1F65, or S1F13, respectively.
Equipment Constant "CONFIGEVENTS" (VID 47) selects which message the Equipment will send for Event Reports. If "ConfigEvents" is 0, the Equipment will send S6F9 for normal (unannotated) event reports or S6F3 for annotated event reports. If "ConfigEvents" is 1, the Equipment will send S6F11 for normal event reports or S6F13 for annotated event reports.
--[p445]-- Equipment Constant "WBITS6" (VID 49) selects whether Stream 6 primary messages (S6F1, S6F3, S6F9, S6F11, and S6F13) sent by the Equipment will have the W-bit set to "0" or "1".
· Equipment Constant "WBITS10" (VID 50) selects whether Stream 10 primary message S10F1 sent by the Equipment will have the W-bit set to "0" or "1".
· Equipment Constant "CONFIGSPOOL" (VID 53) configures whether the Equipment will transition to "Spool Active" state when a RTY error occurs.

===== [p481-482] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.12.2.3 HOST READS SPOOLED DATA (4块) =====
--[p481]-- If not, then the Equipment removes the message from the spool and discards it.
If a transmission failure occurs while attempting to send the spool, the event SPOOLTRANSMITFAILURE (CEID 5007) is sent to the spool and spooling will remain active. While the spool is active, any new (spoolable) messages generated by the Equipment are also sent to the spool.
When the spool has been completely transmitted, the event SpoolingDeactivated (CEID 5006) is sent to the Host.
--[p481]-- 5.12.2.3 HOST READS SPOOLED DATA
The Host can read spooled messages by sending the S6F23 message. Upon receipt of this message, the Equipment will reply and attempt to send spooled messages. Messages are sent in order of oldest to newest, with no priority given to a particular kind of message. The EC MAXSPOOLTRANSMIT (VID 136) determines the maximum number of spooled messages which are sent per S6F23 message received from the Host.
--[p482]-- Instead of reading spooled messages, the Host can purge the spool by sending S6F23 with RSDC = 1. For details, please see section "S6F23 -- Request Spooled Data".
--[p481]-- If zero, all spooled messages are sent, if any other number, that number of messages are sent.
During the de-spooling of messages, the Equipment maintains only one outstanding Equipment-Initiated transaction. The equipment will wait for either a reply to the primary or a T3 timeout before starting another transaction. If the de-spooled message requires a inquire/grant scenario, the Equipment will initiate this transaction first. If the Host accepts the inquire, the message is sent.

===== [p478-479] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.9 Equipment Terminal Services (3块) =====
--[p479]-- Collection Event S10Ack (CEID 12) occurs once the operator has acknowledged the message and an Event Report will be sent to the Host (if enabled).
The S10F3 and S10F9 are restricted to a single TEXT data item, but S10F5 can contain multiple TEXT data items. Each TEXT data item is limited to 160 characters. Each data item in S10F5 will be displayed on a separate line at the equipment.
--[p478]-- 5.9 Equipment Terminal Services
The 7AF supports exchange of free text messages with the Host (SECS Stream 10). This Equipment accepts the following messages from the Host, and responds accordingly if the W-Bit is set to 1:
S10F3 /\* Single Line Data \*/
S10F5 /\* Multi-Line Data \*/
S10F9 /\* Broadcast \*/
The message text will be displayed on the Equipment's CRT.
--[p479]-- If the Operator has not acknowledged an existing message when the Host sends another message, the new message will be displayed and the old one discarded.
The Host can send a message with a 0-length text to clear the Operator text display.
Also, the Equipment allows the operator to send a single block message to the Host via S10F1. The maximum length of this text is 160 characters. The S10F2 response from the Host is ignored.

===== [p469-469] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.5.4 Host Requests Alarm Status (1块) =====
--[p469]-- 5.5.4 Host Requests Alarm Status
The Host can use S5F5 to request the 7AF to report all alarms which exist and the ON/OFF state for each.
The Host can use S5F7 which is similar, but which causes the Equipment to report only those alarms (ALIDs) which are Enabled, regardless of whether the alarm is ON or OFF.

===== [p401-401] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK > Training (3块) =====
--[p401]-- After January 2, 1990, whenever replacement or major modification of a machine or equipment is performed, and whenever new machines or equipment are installed, energy isolating devices for such machines or equipment shall be designed to accept a lockout device [29 CFR 1910.147 (c)(2)(iii)].
--[p401]-- Training
Employees will be trained by an authorized employee [29 CFR 1910.147 (C)(7)(I)]. The affected employees shall be instructed in the purpose and use of the energy control procedure and all other employees whose work operations are or may be in an area where energy control procedures may be used. When tagouts are used, employees must be instructed in the limitations of these devices.
--[p401]-- All authorized and affected employees shall be retrained whenever there is a change in their job assignments, a change in machines, equipment or processes that present a new hazard, or when there is a change in the energy control procedures.

===== [p469-470] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.6.1 Equipment Management of Process Programs (3块) =====
--[p469 [表]]-- The Upper and lower case alphabetic characters are not considered distinct, and the 7AF will not distinguish between them. The File names and extensions are categorized as follows:
Table 18 Recipe File Categorization
File Name | Extension | Recipe Description
Any | .wfr | Wafer
$^ { 6 6 } \mathrm { C o a r s e } ^ { 3 , }$ | .cwd | Coarse Wheel Dress
“Fine&quot; | .fwd | Fine Wheel Dress
“Chuck&quot; | .wcd | Chuck Grind
--[p469]-- 5.6.1 Equipment Management of Process Programs
The 7AF provides a Process Program Library, implemented as a set of binary files maintained on a hard disk. Each Process Program is identified by a unique Process Program ID (PPID). Each PPID is structured as a DOS file name, consisting of up to 12 significant ASCII characters. The first 8 or less characters make up the file name. The next 3 or 4 characters are the DOS extension which begins with a “.” character.
--[p470]-- The Equipment Operator may modify any one of the Process Programs stored on the Equipment. The host will be notified via the PPCHANGEEVENT (CEID 5001) Collection Event if the Operator creates, changes, or deletes a Process Program. The Equipment Operator can also select a PPID to be uploaded to the Host (S7F3), or download from the Host (S7F5).

===== [p498-499] SECS / GEM Interface > 6.25 S2F23 - Trace initialize send (4块) =====
--[p499]-- Up to four (4) separate TRIDs can be in operation simultaneously.
Within DSPER, must be a valid hour/minute/second format ( hh 0-23, mm 0-59, ss 0-59), and cannot be 000000. The practical minimum value of DSPER is application dependent.
The Equipment will send the first S6F1 at one time period (DSPER \* REPGSZ) after receiving S2F23.
If TOTSMP is zero, then S2F23 is a request to cancel an existing trace. Any trace with the specified TRID is canceled.
REPGSZ minimum value is 1.
--[p499]-- REPGSZ may not be so large that S6F1 would be a multi-block message. Typical value is 1.
Several SVIDs can be specified if desired. You must not specify so many SVIDs that S6F1 becomes a multi-block message.
Normally, only Variables of class SV are used in this message. However, any VID of class DV, EC, or SV can be used.
For compatibility with older Host implementations, the Equipment allows the following alternative form for this message, using an array format:
S2F23 W \* H->E
--[p498]-- 6.25 S2F23 - Trace initialize send
S2F23 W \* H->E <L [5] <U4 TRID> \* Trace ID <A 'hhmmss'> \* DSPER - Data Sample Period <U4 TOTSMP> \* Total Number of Samples
7AF SECS/GEM Interface Ver. 1.9
The Host requests the Equipment to initiate a time driven trace operation.
The Equipment will send trace data using S6F1.
If TRID in S2F23 matches TRID of an existing trace, the existing trace operation is canceled, and replaced by the new one.
--[p499]-- <U4 TRID> \* Trace ID
<A 'hhmmss'> \* DSPER - Data Sample Period
<U4 TOTSMP> \* Total Number of Samples
<U4 REPGSZ> \* Reporting Group Size
<U4 SVID ...> \* Status Variable ID array
> .

===== [p492-492] SECS / GEM Interface > 6.5 S1F3 - Selected Status Request (1块) =====
--[p492]-- 6.5 S1F3 - Selected Status Request
The Host requests status from the 7AF. The Host sends the VIDs of interest. Several VIDs can be specified if desired.
Normally, only VIDs of class SV (i.e. Status Variables) are used in this message. However, the 7AF allows the Host to use any VID of class DV, EC, or SV.
If S1F3 contains a zero-length list, then the 7AF will report all variables of class SV, in order by VID.
For compatibility with older Host implementations, the Equipment allows the following alternative form for this message using an array format:

===== [p481-481] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.12.2.2 EQUIPMENT SPOOLS MESSAGES (3块) =====
--[p481]-- 5.12.2.2 EQUIPMENT SPOOLS MESSAGES
While spooling messages, the Equipment will increment the GEMSPOOLCOUNTACTUAL (VID 254) and SPOOLCOUNTTOTAL (VID 250) status variables for each message spooled. Messages which require an inquire/grant scenario are spooled along with the inquire message as a single message.
--[p481]-- That is, if a multi-block S6F11 (Event Report) message is being sent to the Host and spooling is active, the S6F5 (inquire) as well as the S6F1 are sent to the spool and SPOOLCOUNTTOTAL (VID 250) and SPOOLCOUNTACTUAL (VID 249) are incremented by one.
The 7AF maintains two Equipment Constants which effect the spooling of messages. The first is CONFIGSPOOL (VID 53). If this is set to zero, then spooling will never become active.
--[p481]-- If it is set to one, spooling will become active when a transmission failure occurs.
The EC OVERWRITESPOOL (VID 54) determines if the Equipment should over-write the oldest messages with new ones when the spool becomes full. If OVERWRITESPOOL is TRUE, old messages will be over-written with new ones. If FALSE, new messages will be discarded when the spool is full.

===== [p474-475] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.7.5 Setting Process Program and Lot ID’s (16块) =====
--[p475]-- If this happens, the 7AF will assume that new material has been presented and attach the “Next Lot ID” to all material in the cassette. This may not be the correct Lot Id. The host can monitor the “material received” (CE ID #24 and #26) collection events for spurious, unexpected events. Note that sending a PP change to a different recipe during a grind cycle will lock the send cassettes and keep the material from being processed.
--[p474]-- This process can be visualized as the cassette and all material in it being “labeled” with the “Next Lot ID” at the time it is put onto the send turret. Care must be taken to set the PP and Lot Id before setting the cassette of material onto a send turret. Error detection and recovery strategies will be discussed later.
--[p475]-- If the S2F41 message was successful, the line will read “PPID SET.” If the S2F41 message was not successful, the line will read “PPID NOT SET.” Another confirmation would be to check the variables, “Next Lot ID” (VID #25) and “Next Recipe (PP) to Use” (VID #26) by generating a report through GEM.
Limitations: There are some limitations in setting the PP and Lot Ids. First, once a grind cycle has been started, the host cannot change the PP.
--[p475]-- If an invalid parameter was specified in the S2F41 message, the S2F42 response will list the invalid parameter(s) name and the reason that each parameter was considered to be invalid.
The operator can confirm that the message was accepted by looking at the GEM status line in the upper right corner of the screen.
--[p475]-- The recipe name must be a valid DOS file name and present on the 7AF. The 7AF will respond with a S2F42 message. If the S2F41 message is successful, S2F42 will have a HCACK (Host Command Acknowledge) = 0. However, if the message is not successful, S2F42 will have a HCACK equal to a non-zero value which explains why the command was rejected.
--[p474]-- 5.7.5 Setting Process Program and Lot ID’s
To set the Process Program (PP), the operator must notify the host system that material is ready to load onto the machine before setting a cassette onto the send turret. The host will then issue a “PP-SELECT” command that contains the name of the recipe to be used and the Lot Id of the batch to be processed.
--[p475]-- The host can check that the proper sequence is followed by insuring that no material is presented to the machine by monitoring the “material received” (CE ID #24 and #26) collection events before the recipe is requested from the host at a terminal. If this occurs, check the appropriate “Turret Status” variable (VID #29 and #31) to see if a cassette is present.
--[p475]-- This could be used as a strategy to avoid material with the wrong Lot Id from being presented to the robot.
Error Detection and Recovery Strategies: Some steps will be discussed that can be used to confirm that procedures are being followed properly and that information has been transmitted correctly. Simple steps will be discussed first, with increasingly sophisticated strategies later. There are a wealth of tools available through GEM and you may derive other strategies to suit your process.
--[p475]-- If an attempt is made to change the PP during a grind cycle, the request will be denied, the send turrets will be locked to prevent material being presented to the robot and a notice will be presented to the operator notifying them that the turrets have been locked due to an attempted change.
Before a grind cycle is started, the PP can be freely changed. This means that care must be taken to not change the PP once material has been set onto the send turret.
--[p475]-- If material has already been presented, send a message to the operator to immediately stop the cycle. Material may need to be cleared from the machine, but wafers will not be ground with an incorrect PP.
--[p475]-- First, operator training should include double checking the PP (recipe). Also, the operator can check the GEM status line to confirm that the command was accepted. The operator can be assisted in this effort by the host. If an error or problem is detected in setting the PP, the host can send a message to the operator through the S10F3/S10F4 Terminal Display feature.
--[p475]-- This could result in material being processed with the wrong recipe (PP). Operators could be trained to note if the PP changes when presenting material to the machine and not start the grind cycle until the discrepancy is resolved. See below for other ideas on how to use GEM to check this.
Once a cassette is placed on a send turret, it must not be removed and replaced.
--[p474]-- This action can be confirmed through the status received from GEM and by generating a report to check the “Next Lot ID” (VID #25) and “Next Recipe (PP) to Use” (VID #26) variables. The operator will then set the cassette of material (wafers) onto a send turret. When the material is received at the turret, the “Next Lot ID” is associated with the material in the cassette and will follow them throughout the process.
--[p475]-- Check if the operator did not comply before starting the machine by monitoring the “Process State Changed” (CE ID #31) or “Start Wafer Grind Cycle” (CE ID #41) collection events, and the “Process State” variable (VID #15). If the operator has not complied and the turret is not already turned, the turrets can be locked by sending a different PP, stopping the material from being presented to the robot.
--[p475]-- If so, use through the S10F3/S10F4 Terminal Display feature to tell the operator to remove the material and request that the host set up the PP and Lot Id. Likewise, the host can check that the operator does indeed present material immediately after requesting that the PP and Lot Id are set up.
--[p474]-- Procedure to Send the “PP-SELECT” Command: In this example, it will be assumed that the operator has requested that the host set the Process Program by an entry at a host terminal. Given that communication has been established and the 7AF is On Line, the necessary commands can be issued. At this point the Host
should send a S2F41 message to the 7AF containing the remote command, “PP-SELECT”, the Lot Id to be used and the recipe name to be used. The Lot Id is up to 12 ASCII characters.

===== [p462-462] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.3.1.2.3 E10 Non-Productive/Scheduled Downtime (1块) =====
--[p462]-- 5.3.1.2.3 E10 Non-Productive/Scheduled Downtime
The Equipment is scheduled to be out of production so that maintenance can be performed. This state is primarily reflected in the 7AF standby state (VID 17 = 5), but may include other states if the host’s information determines that the machine is scheduled to be “checked out” to maintenance. Care must be taken that when the machine is run by maintenance for test cases, the Productive state (VID 17 = 6) is not counted toward E10 Productive time.

===== [p498-498] SECS / GEM Interface > 6.24 S2F22 - Remote Command Acknowledge (1块) =====
--[p498 [表]]-- 6.24 S2F22 - Remote Command Acknowledge
S2F22 \* H<-E <B [1] CMDA> . \* Command Ack. Code
Normal completion returns a zero (0) in CMDA.
A non-zero value for CMDA indicates that the Equipment has rejected the Remote Command.
CMDA | Description
0x00 | OK. All normal.
0x01 | Invalid command. Equipment rejects command
0x02 | Cannot perform now. Equipment rejects command.
0x40 | Control State is Local. Equipment rejects command.
0x41 | Incorrect Process State for this command.
Equipmentrejects command.

===== [p401-401] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK > Removal of Lockout/Tagout Devices (2块) =====
--[p401]-- Removal of Lockout/Tagout Devices
Before lockout or tagout devices are removed, the authorized employee shall ensure that non-essential items are removed and machine components are operationally intact. The area should be checked to ensure all employees are safely positioned or removed and all affected employees notified that lockout/tagout devices have been removed. The lockout/tagout device must be removed by the person who applied the device.
--[p401]-- If the person who applied the device is not available, the device may be removed by another employee if the employer has established a specific procedure and training for this. When group lockout/tagout devices are used, a procedure equivalent to the personal lockout/tagout system should be followed [29 CFR 1910.147 (f) (3)].

===== [p490-491] SECS / GEM Interface > 6.1 SML Notation (7块) =====
--[p490]-- The count may be omitted, in which case the square brackets are also omitted.
The "count" specifies the number of value elements in the Data Item Value. For String formats (ASCII, Binary, JIS-8), "count" specifies the number of characters in the string. For Numeric formats (I1, I2, I4, I8, U1, U2, U4, U8, F4, F8, BOOLEAN), "count" specifies the number of values in the array. For simple scalar numeric values, "count" is usually "1".
--[p490]-- For example, ASCII values are shown as characters enclosed in quotes, Unspecified Binary values are shown in hexadecimal.
Ellipsis (...) is used to indicate additional elements may occur, as for example where substructures may repeat in a List structure.
As an example, a two-byte unsigned integer Data Item with an array of three values 21, 22, and 23 is represented as: <U2 [3] 21 22 23>
Numeric values shown are considered decimal integers unless otherwise indicated.
--[p490]-- For LIST items, "count" specifies the number of items in the list.
If "count" is omitted, then the length of the Data Item is implied by the value which follows. The "count" can range between known limits. It may be specified as minimum and maximum "counts", separated by two dots. (For example, [0..40]).
value Value of a single item element. Values are shown in a notation that depends on the item type.
--[p491]-- If the W-Bit is optional, it is coded within brackets "[W]".
item An item that is formatted as described above.
A period (.) ends the message definition.
For example, the S1F3 message might be described in SML as follows:
--[p491]-- negative values shown with a leading minus sign "-". Hexadecimal values are shown in C-Language convention, with a leading "0x".
10 Decimal Ten
0x10 Hexadecimal 10
-10 Decimal Negative 10
Where a value is not fixed, the SECS variable name is used directly. For Example:
<A [6] SOFTREV>
The format of a complete message is:
SnFn W item .
The components are:
SnFn The Stream and Function Codes, S1F1 for example.
W The W-Bit, if set. Omitted if not set.
--[p490 [表]]-- This notation implies that each Data Item has a Data Item Format and Data Item Length as required by SECS-II.
type This specifies the SECS-II Data Item format. It will have one of the following values:
A | ASCII
B | Binary
J | JIS-8
I1, I2, I4, I8 | Signed Integers
U1, U2, U4, U8 Unsigned Integers
F4, F8 | Floating Point
BOOLEAN | True/False
count Count of the element values that make up the item. If present, the count is enclosed within square brackets "[ ]".
--[p490]-- 6.1 SML Notation
Message descriptions are shown using "SECS Message Language" (SML) notation. SML is a general notation developed by GW Associates for describing SECS messages. SML is similar to the notation used in the SECS Standards documents, but SML is a more precise and regular notation. In SML, the format for a data item is as follows:
< type [ count ] value >
The components are:
<> Angle Brackets. Each Data Item is enclosed within angle brackets ("less than", "greater than").

===== [p441-441] SECS / GEM Interface > 3.2.5 Simultaneous Transactions (2块) =====
--[p441]-- The Host can reduce the number of outstanding transactions initiated by the Equipment by setting Equipment Constants appropriately so that the Equipment sends no W-Bit for Stream 5 (Alarm), Stream 6 (Event), and Stream 10 (Free Text) messages.
The Equipment allows the Host to initiate at least two (2) simultaneous outstanding transactions.
--[p441]-- 3.2.5 Simultaneous Transactions
The 7AF may initiate several simultaneous outstanding SECS transactions. That is, the Equipment may send a secondary primary message before the Host has sent the Reply to a previous primary message. Mainly, this occurs when the Equipment reports Alarms and Events.

--[p492]-- 6.4 S1F2 - On Line Data (Host to Equipment)

===== [p468-468] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.5.2 Reporting (2块) =====
--[p468]-- The equipment has two CEIDs for each ALID, one for the "going on" transition and one for the "going off" transition. In addition to the Alarm Report, the Equipment sends an Event Report if the CEID associated with the alarm change is enabled. If the CEID is enabled and no report is defined, a "null" Event Report is sent. The event report for an alarm transition is sent if it is enabled, even if the reporting for the alarm is disabled.
--[p468]-- 5.5.2 Reporting
The 7AF reports alarms to the Host when they occur, without Host action, using the alarm report message S5F1 or configurable option, depending on CONFIGALARMS (VID 46). The transition of an ALID from OFF to ON is referred to as "going on" or "leading edge", and the transition from ON to OFF as "going off" or "trailing edge". The Equipment reports both leading and trailing edge transitions.

===== [p403-403] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK > PRESSURIZED AIR IN (1块) =====
--[p403]-- PRESSURIZED AIR IN
Connect clean, dry house air (80-120 psi) to the connection marked Clean Dry Air on the front control panel. The safety lockout valve (265648) is on this line.
The pilot pressure regulator passes air at 80 psi to the purge pressure regulator, and through solenoid 2 to the three pneumatically operated valves.

===== [p474-474] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.7.4 Remote Grinding Operations (5块) =====
--[p474]-- 5.7.4 Remote Grinding Operations
To prepare the 7AF for remote control grinding of product, certain steps must be taken in order. First, the command, BEGIN-AUTO, must be successfully executed. This will put the 7AF in Process State 2, Grind Screen Wait For Start. This should be confirmed by checking that VID 15 is indeed equal to 2. Next, the grind process must be selected by issuing the GRIND-TYPE command with an argument of COARSE, FINE, or DUAL.
--[p474]-- The process can be restarted with a START command. If the 7AF stops due to a fault or intervention by the host with a STOP or ESTOP command, product can be left in the equipment and will need to be manually unloaded. Product’s location can be checked in VID 37. Any product in the equipment must be cleared or product will be damaged. Stopping of the process by any means other than exhausting the product being put into the equipment should result in a careful inspection before proceeding.
--[p474]-- This should be confirmed by checking that VID 27 (0 = None; 1 = Coarse; 2 = Fine; 3 = Both) matches your choice. The machine is ready to accept a PP and material to begin. For a discussion about managing PP loading, see section 5.7.6 below. When the PP and product are loaded, the 7AF is ready to start.
Processing is started by issuing the START command. When product is exhausted and the process is stopping (Process State VID 15 = 20), the host should acknowledge with a STOP command.
--[p474]-- The PAUSE command can be used to pause the process and allow any product being actively processed to be finished (reference VID 38, 39). The process can be stopped with a STOP command when the Coarse and Fine Spindle Status (VID 38, 39) has reached the Idle (-2) state. Product will not be moved and must be manually cleared. The process can be restarted with the START command.
--[p474]-- Alternatively, the process can be restarted after all turrets have been rotated to not allow more product into the machine. This will allow all product to be cleared automatically, with the possible processing of one piece of product from the prealigner.

===== [p469-469] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.6 Process Program Management (1块) =====
--[p469]-- 5.6 Process Program Management
Processing on the 7AF is controlled by Process Programs. The Equipment requires selection of a Process Program for each process. The 7AF supports the use of unformatted process programs.

===== [p454-454] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.2.1 Control Finite State Description (1块) =====

===== [p398-398] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK > Preparation for Lockout (1块) =====
--[p398]-- Preparation for Lockout
Maintenance personnel authorized to perform lockout shall be certain as to which switch, valve or other energy isolating devices apply to the equipment being locked out. More than one energy source (electrical, mechanical, or others) may be involved. Employees shall clarify the identification of questionable sources with their supervisors. Before lockout commences, job authorization should be obtained.

===== [p472-472] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.7.1.3 PAUSE (1块) =====

The PAUSE command will cause the 7AF to complete the processing of wafers currently in process, but not to start any new wafers until the RESUME command has been given. The process may be aborted with the “STOP” or “ESTOP” command.

===== [p453-453] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.1.1.2.2.1 COMMUNICATING (2块) =====
--[p453]-- If the Equipment encounters a SECS-I Retry Limit (RTY) error when attempting to send a block to the host, it discards any messages queued for send and the communication state transits to ENABLED.
--[p453]-- 5.1.1.2.2.1 COMMUNICATING
The SECS link between the 7AF and the Host is operating normally.
Periodically, the Equipment will send a "Heartbeat" message S1F1 to ensure that the link is still operating. The heartbeat frequency is controlled by Equipment Constant HEARTBEAT. HEARTBEAT (VID 51) can range from 0 to 32000, with default value 30.

===== [p479-479] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.11 Clock (2块) =====
--[p479]-- 5.11 Clock
The 7AF contains Clock/Calendar hardware, by which it knows the current date and time.
The Host can send S2F31 to set the Equipment's Clock/Calendar hardware.
The Host can send S2F17 to read the Equipment's Clock/Calendar hardware.
The Operator can initiate a Date/Time request from the Host. The Equipment will send S2F17 to the Host and will set its clock according to the data in the S2F18 reply.
--[p479]-- Note that the Host generated command to update the clock will only be accepted when the Process State (VID 15) is “0”, or when the operator is in the GEM Maintenance screen.

===== [p480-480] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.12 Spooling (2块) =====
--[p480]-- 5.12 Spooling
When the SECS link between the Host and the 7AF goes down (RTY error on the Equipment side), the 7AF will spool appropriate messages so that the Host can read them once the link comes back up (after a successful Connect Request transaction).
The Host can set spooling attributes on the 7AF by setting certain Equipment Constants with the S2F15/16 transaction.
The Host can define streams and functions of messages to be spooled through the S2F43/44 transaction.
--[p480]-- Stream one (S1Fx) messages are not eligible for spooling. The Host can also disable spooling for messages through this S2F43/44 transaction. Stream 9 messages are not spooled.
The Host may read spooled messages or purge the Equipment's spool through the S6F23/24 transaction.

===== [p390-391] Universal Vacuum System > GENERAL INFORMATION (5块) =====
--[p391]-- Pregnant women, in particular, should heed this advice. Closing cabinet effectively shields all personnel from any perceived hazardous fields. Studies are being conducted by the U. S. Department of Energy to determine what risks, if any, are posed by low frequency electromagnetic field exposure.
• Always consult with your supervisor if your task or procedure is unclear or if you believe that your assignment could result in unsafe conditions or equipment damage.
--[p390]-- Interlocks and other safety circuits or devices may not be overridden except by trained maintenance personnel using approved procedures. Operators must not override interlocks or safety devices under any circumstances.
• Disconnect power when servicing or repairing the machine.
• DO NOT operate the machine without proper electrical grounding.
• DO NOT wear loose clothing that could be caught by machine parts in motion.
• Wear SAFETY GLASSES when working near moving machinery.
--[p390]-- It is the responsibility of the user to be sure that the machine is in safe operating condition at all times. The user is also responsible for insuring that operators and maintenance personnel follow approved operating and maintenance procedures. The following is a list of safety instructions:
DO NOT put hands or objects inside the UVS cabinet while the machine is poweredup or in operation.
• Keep all guards and covers in place and in good repair.
--[p390]-- • Always heed visual hazard alert labels and messages.
Recommendation Only: Avoid long-term exposure to low frequency electromagnetic fields. The data concerning low-frequency electromagnetic health effects is inconclusive, but a 1995 IEEE engineering publication recommends “prudent avoidance” of prolonged and continuous exposure. Maintenance personnel are advised to avoid standing at open power panel doors for extended periods with the power on.
--[p390]-- GENERAL INFORMATION
Strasbaugh machines are designed for safe operation. However, caution must be exercised when operating this machine. Failure to adhere to these safety instructions and to good safety practices in general may result in personal injury or in damage to the machine. Hearing protection should not be necessary, since the UVS produces less than 70 db(A) sound pressure during normal operation.

===== [p467-467] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.4.7 Disk Files (1块) =====
--[p467]-- 5.4.7 Disk Files
The 7AF maintains a disk file which contains the current Equipment Constant settings. The file is updated each time the Operator or Host changes an Equipment Constant. The most recent settings for some of the Equipment Constants are read from the file when the Equipment is powered-on.

===== [p458-458] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.2.2 Power Up (1块) =====
--[p458]-- 5.2.2 Power Up
At Power Up, the Equipment Constant INITCONTROLSTATE (VID 41) controls whether ControlState is initialized to ONLINE or OFFLINE. Within the Off-Line super-state, the Equipment Constant OFFLINESUBSTATE (VID 42) controls whether the Control State defaults to:
1. Equipment Off-Line
2. Host Off-Line
3. Attempt On-Line
If INITCONTROLSTATE (VID 41) initializes to On-Line, the variable ONLINESUBSTATE (VID 44) determines whether the default state is:
4. Local
5. Remote

===== [p475-475] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.8 Material Movement (2块) =====
--[p475]-- 5.8 Material Movement
Material movement on the 7AF consists of three components: 1) The input cassette; 2) the output cassette; and 3) The Equipment. In order for processing to begin, a cassette of wafers must be placed on the input port and an empty cassette on the output port. The 7AF then takes wafers from the input cassette, processes them and then places them in the output cassette. Before a new lot can be started, these cassettes must be removed and replaced with empty/full cassettes.
--[p475]-- The following diagrams depict the state transitions for the input and output ports on the 7AF. Any state transition which occurs for the input ports, (CEIDs 23, 24, 25, 26) will be sent to the Host if enabled. Any state transition which occurs for the output ports will trigger the appropriate collection events (CEID 27, 28, 29, 30).

===== [p447-447] SECS / GEM Interface > 3.10 Modifying Equipment Constants from the 7AF Console (2块) =====
--[p447]-- 3.10 Modifying Equipment Constants from the 7AF Console
The following steps should be taken to modify an Equipment Constant from the 7AF Console:
1. Exit the 7AF application and to return to the DOS prompt.
2. Using a text editor, such as EDIT, open the file EC\_DEFLT.TXT.
3. This file contains several lines of text, each line containing the VID of an Equipment Constant, and that EC’s current setting.
--[p447]-- Refer to Appendix A of this document to determine the VID of the Equipment Constant that you want to modify.
4. Using the text editor, modify the current setting field of the Equipment Constant, indexed my VID.
5. Save the file EC\_DEFLT.TXT.
6. Reboot the 7AF computer to restart the 7AF application.

===== [p440-440] SECS / GEM Interface > 3.1 SECS Standard (1块) =====
--[p440]-- 3.1 SECS Standard
The SEMI Equipment Communication Standard (SECS) is published by Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International (SEMI). It defines a computer to computer communications interface between a unit of factory Equipment and a Host Computer.
This Equipment complies to the complete SECS-I standard, and to the generic portions of the SECS-II standard, and implements an appropriate subset of the SECS-II standard messages. The 7AF complies to the following versions of standards:
1.
E4-0298 (SECS-I)
Note: There were no changes to the SEMI E4 standard for 1993.
2. E50298 (SECS-II)

===== [p395-395] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK (2块) =====
--[p395]-- POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK
The Universal Vacuum System has three independent safety systems consisting of an Emergency Shutoff button, the Power Interlock on the front panel and the Lock-out/Purge valve for air pressure. Machine operation cannot be restarted until the EMERGENCY OFF button is pulled or twisted clockwise to the OUT position. The Machine On button must then be pushed to restart the machine.
--[p395]-- Notes: To shut down the machine for any extended period, press the EMO and then disconnect facilities power to the machine.
The Power Interlock on the front panel prevents opening the machine cabinet without first shutting off machine power. The power interlock may be locked in the OFF position and used as part of an established lock-out procedure.
The Pneumatic lock-out/Purge valve is located behind the lower control panel in the center and may be locked in the OFF position.
A red flag should be used when this valve is locked-out since the valve itself is not visible from the front of the machine.

===== [p480-480] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.12.1 A Word of Caution (3块) =====
--[p480]-- 5.12.1 A Word of Caution
If the Host does not intend to use the spooling features of the Equipment, the Equipment Constant ConfigSpool (VID 53) should be set to zero. Setting this EC to zero disables the spooling feature. If this is not set to zero, and the Host does not support spooling, the SECS connection with the Equipment will be crippled. This happens because of the following:
1.
--[p480]-- Therefore, if your Host does not support spooling and spooling becomes active, you will never again receive non stream 1 messages from the Equipment. If this occurs, you will need to use a Host simulator such as SECSIM to delete the spool.
If the Host does not intend to use the spooling features of the 7AF, CONFIGSPOOL (VID 53) should be set to zero. This will disable the spooling feature and the Equipment will never transition to Spool Active state.
After a transition is made to Spool Active, the only way to get out of the state is to read or purge the spool.
--[p480]-- When spooling becomes active (transmission error), the Equipment will not send non-stream 1 primary messages to the Host. That is, it will not send, events, alarms, process programs, terminal display, etc.
2. When spooling becomes active, the ONLY way to deactivate it is to read or delete the spool from the Host. In complying with the GEM standard, the Equipment does not have the ability to reset its spooling state.
3.

===== [p391-391] Universal Vacuum System > HAZARDS INHERENT IN DEVICE (1块) =====
--[p391]-- HAZARDS INHERENT IN DEVICE
The machine is moderately heavy. It should remain upright and not be dropped. During transport it should be secured so as not to impact other objects.
The machine is tall with a narrow footprint. It should not be set down in such a way as to break through the floor surface or cause any floor sagging that could throw it out of level. It should be placed and secured so that there is no foreseeable danger of tipping over in an earthquake, flood, fire or other accident.
See Seismic Protection section.

The Strasbaugh Universal Vacuum System is designed to provide a dependable and steady source of vacuum suitable for the proper operation of Strasbaugh equipment as well as other equipment requiring reliable vacuum.

===== [p485-485] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.12.4.4 Spool Active (1块) =====

While GemConfigSpool (VID 53) is "enabled" ("1"), the 7AF has experienced a transmission failure (RTY error). Upon entry into this state, the first message sent to the spool is the GemSpoolingActivated event (CEID 5005), assuming that this event is enabled and that spooling for the particular stream and function have been enabled. This message will enter the spool even before the message which originally caused the RTY error.

===== [p406-406] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK > Overview of Purge Mode (1块) =====
--[p406]-- Overview of Purge Mode
When the drain tank fills with water, the upper float triggers a purge cycle, isolating the vacuum tank from the drain tank, and draining the drain tank. As the water level falls, the lower float turns the purge cycle off and the system is restored to normal mode.

===== [p465-465] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.3.4.3 Grind Cycle States (VID 15 = 2, 3, 9, 20, 21) (1块) =====
--[p465]-- 5.3.4.3 Grind Cycle States (VID 15 = 2, 3, 9, 20, 21)
Grinding is monitored through the Grind Cycle States. Waiting for material processing to start is State 2. Processing of material is reflected by State 9. If the process is paused, State 21 is active. If the process is being stopped, State 20 is active. Note that State 20 is shared by all grind-like processes to signify a transitional state.
When a process has been stopped because material to process has been exhausted or an operator has intervened, Wait for Quit, State 3, is entered.

===== [p408-408] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK > VACUUM (2块) =====
--[p408]-- VACUUM
The vacuum switch is an SMC switch (part 226044). This switch is adjusted at the factory to turn on the vacuum pump when vacuum reaches 20 inches of mercury and to turn off the pump when vacuum reaches 25 inches of mercury.
Adjust this switch if the vacuum does not remain between the desired settings.
The switch is set at the factory. To recalibrate this switch:
1. Hold the SET button until the units flash.
2. Press the DOWN key until the display shows units as psi.
3.
--[p408 [表]]-- Press the SET button (locks units and enters mode setting).
4. Pres the SET button again until P1 is displayed.
5. Press the UP/DOWN keys unil P1 is set to –10.1.
6. Press the SET button to adjust P2 to –11.2.
7. Press the SET button to finish (return the switch to normal mode).
Setting | Mode | in. Hg. | psi
ON | P1 | 20 | - 10.1
OFF | P2 | 25 | - 11.2

===== [p405-405] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK > NORMAL OPERATING MODE (1块) =====
--[p405]-- NORMAL OPERATING MODE
During normal operations, water is drained from the vacuum tank to the drain tank by gravity, since both are under equal pressure (vacuum). Air pressure, regulated to 80 psi by the pilot pressure regulator, is routed through solenoid 2 and activates all three pneumatic valves (see diagram).

===== [p493-493] SECS / GEM Interface > 6.9 S1F13 - Connect Request (1块) =====

The Equipment sends this message using the following format.
The Host sends this message using the following format.
S1F13 W \* H->E <L> .

===== [p466-466] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.4.1 Variables (2块) =====
--[p466]-- The Host can read values for Status Variables and Equipment Constants whenever the 7AF is On-Line, but values for Data Variables are typically meaningful only immediately after certain Collection Events (CEIDs), and so are typically reported only in Event Reports (S6F11).
--[p466]-- 5.4.1 Variables
The 7AF has a fixed set of Variables which can be read by the Host. Each Variable is identified by a unique Variable ID (VID). The Variables which exist are shown in "Appendix A -- Variables".
There are three types of Variables: Status Variables, Data Variables, and Equipment Constants. The Host can read Variables of any type, but can set values only for Equipment Constants.

===== [p407-407] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK > Detailed Explanation of Purge Mode (3块) =====
--[p407]-- Solenoid 2 opens, causing the pneumatic valves to simultaneously change back to their normal operating states:
· Valve 1 (between the tanks) opens.
· Valve 2 switches back to vacuum supply.
· Valve 3 (below the drain tank) closes.
--[p407]-- Detailed Explanation of Purge Mode
As water from the vacuum tank drains (by gravity) into the drain tank, both floats rise. When the water rises high enough, the upper switch closes, triggering the following events:
1. Solenoid 2 closes, shutting off pilot pressure to the three valves and causing them to simultaneously changes states:
· Valve 1 (between the two tanks) closes, isolating the drain tank from the vacuum tank.
· Valve 2 closes the vacuum supply line and opens the purge pressure line.
--[p407]-- · Valve 3 (below the drain tank) opens.
2. The drain tank (isolated from the vacuum source) equalizes with atmospheric pressure via the open drain valve.
3. After a short delay, solenoid 1 opens, supplying purge pressure to the drain tank, pumping water out the drain.
4. As the water is drained, the lower float drops. When the float switch closes, solenoid 1 shuts off purge pressure to the drain tank.
5.

2 | S5F1 (AlarmReport 1) | The Alarm Report message is sent to the spool.

===== [p467-467] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.4.6 Time Driven Trace (2块) =====
--[p467]-- all variables requested).
The equipment allows Host definition of trace data to exceed the one-block limit when reported. That is, the SEMI E5 standard states that the S6F1 (Trace Data Send) message is limited to a single SECS block; but the Equipment will allow this point to be overlooked at the Host's request. If the Host does define trace data to be larger than one SECS block, then the Equipment will send the multiple blocks, not preceded by the S6F5/S6F6 Inquire/Grant scenario.
--[p467]-- 5.4.6 Time Driven Trace
The 7AF supports Time Driven Trace initiated from the Host. The Host initializes a trace using S2F23. The Equipment will send the data requested after the specified time interval has expired. The data will be sent using the S6F1 (Trace Data Send) message.
The Equipment can handle several concurrent traces. The number of concurrent traces is determined by the size of the trace data requested. The Equipment can support at least four concurrent traces to a maximum size (i.e.

===== [p465-465] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.3.4.4 Dress and True Cycle States (VID 15 = 4, 5, 12 through 20) (1块) =====
--[p465]-- 5.3.4.4 Dress and True Cycle States (VID 15 = 4, 5, 12 through 20)
Dress and Truing operations are monitored through the Dress and Truing Cycle States. Waiting for an operation to be selected is State 4. The operation selected will be reflected in the state entered, State 12 to State 19. If the operation is being stopped, State 20 is active. Note that State 20 is shared by all grind-like processes to signify a transitional state.
When the chosen operation has been stopped and acknowledged by the operator, Wait for Quit, State 5, is entered.

===== [p457-457] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.2.1.2.4 On-Line/LOCAL (2块) =====
--[p457]-- 5.2.1.2.4 On-Line/LOCAL
The local operator has control of the 7AF. The Host can send S2F41 (Remote Command), but the Equipment will reject any commands that result in movement of the Equipment with 0x40 return code. See "6.42 S2F42 - Remote Command Acknowledge" or section 5.7 "Remote Commands" for details.
In LOCAL mode, the Equipment continues to send Event and Alarm reports to the Host. The Host can monitor operations, but cannot control processing.
--[p457]-- However, the Host can still exert "controls" other than S2F41 which do not directly affect processing. For example, the Host can enable/disable Alarms and set the Clock.

===== [p441-441] SECS / GEM Interface > 3.2.4 Interleaved Blocks (1块) =====
--[p441]-- 3.2.4 Interleaved Blocks
The 7AF never sends interleaved blocks to the Host. That is, the Equipment always sends all blocks of one message before sending the first block of the next message. This simplifies the job of the Host.
However, the Equipment allows the Host to send interleaved blocks, if it so chooses.

===== [p466-466] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.4.3 Host Requests Status (1块) =====

The Host can send S1F3 when the Equipment is On-Line to read Equipment Constants from the 7AF.
The Host can send S2F13 when the Equipment is On-Line to read Equipment Constants from the 7AF.
For this Equipment, S1F3 and S2F13 with a list of VIDs are essentially the same. That is, either message can return Variables of any type. However, S1F3 with a zero-length list will return only VIDs of type SV, and S2F13 with a zerolength list will return only VIDs of type EC.

--[p465]-- 5.3.4 7AF Process States

===== [p462-462] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.3.1.2.4 E10 Non-Productive/Engineering (1块) =====
--[p462]-- 5.3.1.2.4 E10 Non-Productive/Engineering
The Equipment may be running wafers (VID 17 = 6), but these are not intended to be used in normal production. This state signifies that Engineering data is being gathered from the Equipment separate from an actual production run. The host must use its information to be sure that the Productive state (VID 17 = 6) is not counted toward E10 Productive time.

===== [p471-471] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.7.1.1 START (1块) =====
--[p471]-- 5.7.1.1 START
This command starts processing on the 7AF assuming all proper initialization has taken place and material is present. The command, “BEGIN-AUTO”, must be issued successfully to set the 7AF to Process State 2. Also, “GRIND-TYPE” must be successfully issued to select the grind type.
S2F41 [W] <L [2] <A 'START'> <L> > .

===== [p485-485] SECS / GEM Interface > 5.12.4.3 Spool Inactive (1块) =====
--[p485]-- 5.12.4.3 Spool Inactive
Spooling is not activated. This is either because GemConfigSpool (VID 53) is "0" (disabled) in which case, spooling will never be active, or because while GemConfigSpool is enabled ("1"), a RTY error has not occurred. In this state, no messages are sent to the spool. The Host may define or un-define messages eligible for spooling should the link go down.

===== [p399-399] POWER INTERRUPT ANDINTERLOCK > Restoring Equipment to Service (1块) =====
--[p399]-- Restoring Equipment to Service
1. When the job is complete and equipment is ready for testing or normal service, check the equipment area to see that no one is exposed.
2. When equipment is all clear, remove all locks. The energy isolating devices may be operated to restore energy to equipment.

===== [p197-197] Humphrey VACUUM VALVES > 4) Harmonic suppression techniques (3块) =====
--[p197]-- 5 | AC filter | A capacitor and a reactor are used together to reduce impedance at specific frequencies,producing a great effect of absorbing harmonic currents.
6 | Active filter | This filter detects the current of a circuit generating a harmonic current and generates a harmoniccurrent equivalent to a difference between that current and a fundamental wave current tosuppress a harmonic current at a detection point, providing a great effect of absorbing harmoniccurrents.
--[p197 [表]]-- 4) Harmonic suppression techniques
No. | Item | Description
1 | Reactor installation(ACL, DCL) | Install a reactor (ACL) in the AC side of the inverter or a reactor (DCL) in its DC side or both tosuppress outgoing harmonic currents.
2 | High power factorconverter(FR-HC) | The converter circuit is switched on-off to convert an input current waveform into a sine wave,suppressing harmonic currents substantially. The high power factor converter (FR-HC) is usedwith the standard accessory.
--[p197]-- 3 | Installation of powerfactor improvingcapacitor | When used with a series reactor, the power factor improving capacitor has an effect of absorbingharmonic currents
4 | Transformer multi-phase operation | Use two transformers with a phase angle difference of 30° as in Y-∆, ∆-Δ combination to providean effect corresponding to 12 puises, reducing low-degree harmonic currents.

===== [p130-132] HEIDENHAIN-METRO MT 12W/MT 25W > 6. Montage (5块) =====
--[p131]-- Le MT 12W/25W doit être aligné sur la sur face de la table de mesure ou sur l’élément mobile de la machine à l’aide de la surface de référence en-dessous du palpeur, à condition que la surface de fixation ait déjà été confectionnée au préalable perpendiculairement à la surface de la table de mesure ou parallèlement au guidage de la machine.
Allgemein läßt sich der Meßfehler bedingt durch schrägen Anbau nach folgender Formel berechnen:
$$
F = \ L M \times ( \frac { 1 } { \cos \alpha } - 1 )
$$
--[p132]-- En général, l’erreur de mesure causée par un montage oblique peut être calculée d’après la formule suivante:
$$
F = L M \times ( \frac { 1 } { \cos \alpha } - 1 )
$$
dans laquelle:
F = erreur de mesure en mm
LM = course de mesure en mm
α = position oblique du palpeur en degrés d’arc
--[p132]-- mit F = Meßfehler in mm
$$
L _ { \mathsf { M } } = \mathsf { M e B w e g i n } \mathsf { m m }
$$
a = Schrägstellung des Meßtasters in Winkelgrad
In general, the measuring error owing to a biased mounting can be calculated by the following formula:
$$
F = L M \times \left. \frac { \mathcal { 1 } } { c o s \mathrm { \sf ~ d } } - \mathrm { \boldsymbol { \mathit { 1 } } } \right.
$$
with F = measuring error in mm
$$
\angle M = t r a v e / \dot { m } m m
$$
a = bias of gauge head in angular degrees
--[p131]-- Align MT 12W/MT 25W to the measuring table surface or to the moving machine element by means of the reference face on the underside of the gauge head provided that the securing face has been machined perpendicular to the measuring table surface, i. e. parallel to the machine guideway.
--[p130]-- 6. Montage
Le MT 12W/25W est à monter sur une surface plane aux dimensions min. 14 × 59 mm.
Des vis M4 ou M6 peuvent être utilisées pour la fixation.
Position d’utilisation au choix
Mit Hilfe der Referenzfläche an der Tasterunterseite ist der MT 12W/25W zur Meß- tischoberfläche bzw. zum bewegten Maschinenelement auszurichten. Voraussetzung ist, daß die Anschraubfläche bereits entsprechend rechtwinklig zur Meßtischoberfläche bzw. parallel zur Maschinenführung gefertigt wurde.

===== [p20-20] 6.69 S6F11 - Event Report Send (2块) =====
--[p20]-- The Equipment sends one or more Event Reports which the Host has previously linked to that CEID (see S2F35). Each report contains specific Variables which the Host has previously defined for that Report (see S2F33).
The Equipment generates a value for DATAID to uniquely identify this Conversation. If S6F11 is multiblock, the Equipment first sends the S6F5/S6F6 Inquire/Grant transaction, and the DATAID in S6F11 will match DATAID in S6F5.
If the CEID is enabled, but no Reports are linked to this CEID, S6F11 has the following special format:
--[p20]-- 6.69 S6F11 - Event Report Send
This message is the "normal" message that the Equipment uses to report events. In order for this message to be used, the Equipment Constant "ConfigEvents" must be set to "1".
A Collection Event has occurred at the Equipment. The Host has enabled event reporting for this CEID (see S2F37). The Host has set the Equipment Constant RpType to "False" (normal report format desired).

--[p345]-- (6) Speed does not increase.
• Check that the maximum frequency (Pr. 1) setting is correct.
• Check that the load is not too heavy. (In agitators, etc., load may become heavy in winter.)
• Check that the torque boost (Pr. 0, Pr. 46, Pr. 112) setting is not too large to activate the stall prevention function.

===== [p271-329] Pr. 73 "0-5V/0-10V selection" > (1) Parameter setting (7块) =====

--[p271]-- (1) Parameter setting
• Using Pr. 80 and Pr. 81, select the advanced magnetic flux vector control.
• Refer to the parameter details list and set the following parameters:
1) Set "1 or 101" in Pr. 96.
• For setting of "1". Tuning without motor running.
For setting of "101". ... . .· Tuning with motor running
2) Set the rated motor current (A) in Pr. 9.
3) Set the rated motor voltage (V) in Pr. 83.
4) Set the rated motor frequency (Hz) in Pr. 84.
5) Select the motor using Pr. 71.
--[p329]-- ParameterNumber | Name | Setting | Description
278 setting + 3-4Hz.This parameter may only be set if Pr. 282 ≥ Pr. 278.
283 | Brake operation timeat stop | 0 to 5 sec | Pr. 60=7: Set the mechanical delay time until the brake is closed + 0.1seconds.Pr. 60=8: Set the mechanical delay time until the brake is closed + about0.2-0.3 seconds.
284 | Deceleration detectionfunction selection | 0 | Deceleration is not detected.
--[p271]-- · Standard motor Pr. 71 = "3"
Constant-toraue motor ......................· Pr. 71 = "13"
• Mitsubishi standard motor SF-JR 4 poles (1.5kW or less) Pr. 71 = "23"
Note: Pr. 83 and Pr. 84 are only displayed when the advanced magnetic flux vector control is selected (Pr. 80, Pr. 81).
In these parameters, set the values given on the motor plate. When the standard motor has more than one rated value, set 200V/60Hz or 400V/60Hz.
--[p329]-- ParameterNumber | Name | Setting | Description
278 | Brake openingfrequency | 0 to 30Hz | Set to the rated slip frequency of the motor + about 1.0Hz.This parameter may only be set if Pr. 278 ≤ Pr. 282.
279 | Brake opening current | 0 to 200% | Generally, set this parameter to about 50-90%. If the setting is toolow, the load is liable to drop with gravity at start.Suppose that the rated inverter current is 100%
--[p329 [表]]-- (1) Parameter setting
1) Select advanced magnetic flux vector control. (Pr. 80, Pr. 81 ≠"9999")
2) Set "7 or 8" (brake sequence mode) in Pr. 60
To ensure more complete sequence control, it is recommended to set "7" (brake opening completion signal input) in Pr. 60. Note that the automatic restart after instantaneous power failure function is not activated when the brake sequence mode is selected.
3) Refer to the following table and set the parameters

===== [p454-454] MITSUBISHI ELECTRIC CORPORATION > II. DUAL PRESSURE (Type RD) (2块) =====
--[p454]-- II. DUAL PRESSURE (Type RD)
This assembly has two regulators for dual pressure applications. It takes line prēssure from the P port of the base. and supplies it to the input of two regulators. The regulator outputs are supplied to ports EA and EB of the valve unit. Cylinder ports A and B are connected through the regulator back to ports A and B in the base. Common exhaust, now port P in the valve unit, is connected to port EB in the base or manifold.
--[p454]-- Single pressure regulators have a 1/8 NPTF gage port opposite the adiusting knob; double pressure regulators do not have gage ports available. Gages are not furnished with the regulator assemblies. NOTE: On double regulator units, a gage may be temporarily connected in the cylinder port lines to set the drownstream pressure.
Pressure Range: Primary: 150 PSIG Max. Secondary: 5 - 100 PSIG Adjustable

===== [p344-344] CHAPTER 5 PROTECTIVE FUNCTIONS > 3) Check the parameter settings (1块) =====
--[p344]-- 3) Check the parameter settings
• Check that the reverse rotation prevention (Pr. 78) is not selected.
• Check that the operation mode (Pr. 79) setting is correct
• Check that the bias and gain (Pr. 902 to Pr. 905) settings are correct.
• Check that the starting frequency (Pr. 13) setting is not greater than the running frequency
• Check that various operational functions (such as three-speed operation), especially the maximum frequency (Pr. 1), are not zero.
4) Check the load
• Check that the load is not too heavy.
• Check that the shaft is not locked.

===== [p138-138] HEIDENHAIN-METRO MT 12W/MT 25W > 7.8 Exchange of bellows (3块) =====
--[p138]-- 7.8 Exchange of bellows
The bellows of the splashwater-proof gauge MT 12W25W is resistant to ageing.   
weathering, ozone and water; it is conditionally resistant to various mineral oils   
and lubricants, It is easy to replace.   
.unscrew measuring contact   
.pull bellows from upper groove   
.slide bellows off   
.insert new bellows   
Observe correct fitting into upper   
groove!   
insert measuring contact   
Replacement bellows are available from HEIDENHAIN:
--[p138]-- Veiller à une bonne adaptation dans la rainure supérieure!   
.remettre la touche de mesure en la vissant. Les soufflets sont livrables par   
HEIDENHAIN:   
soufflet pour MT 12W   
No. d’ident. 230 58701   
soufflet pour MT 25W   
No. d’ident. 230 58601.
--[p138]-- Bellows for MT 12W Id.-No, 23058701 Bellows for MT 25W Id.-No. 230 586 01 Le soufflet du palpeur étanche   
MT 12W/25W est inaltérable et résiste aux intempéries, l’ozone et l'eau; il résiste, avec certaines restrictions, à différentes huiles et graisses minérales. Son remplacement est très facile:   
.enlever la touche de mesure en la dévissant .retirer le soufflet de la rainure supérieure ,enlever le soufflet   
,remettre le nouveau soufflet.

===== [p290-290] Pr. 73 "0-5V/0-10V selection" > 2) PD action (1块) =====
--[p290]-- 2) PD action
A combination of proportional control action (P) and differential control action (D) for providing a manipulated variable in response to deviation speed to improve the transient characteristic.
[Operation example for proportional changes of process value]
Note: PD action is the sum of P and D actions

===== [p313-313] Pr. 73 "0-5V/0-10V selection" > (Example: Set point No. 1, forward rotation, 30Hz, 4 hours 30 minutes) (3块) =====
--[p313]-- 202), and press the [SET] key ([READ] key when using the FR-PU04 parameter unit) to display the current setting. Hereafter, press the [UP] key to advance the parameter one by one
Note 1: To make a stop, write "0" in the rotation direction and frequency. Set "9999" for no setting.   
Note 2: An error will result if 4.80 is entered (59 minutes or 59 seconds is exceeded).
--[p313 [表]]-- · Assuming that operation has been programmed as indicated in the following table, the operation pattern is as shown in the figure below:
No. | Operation | Parameter Setting
1 | Forward rotation, 20Hz, 1 hour 0minutes | Pr. 201 = 1, 20, 1:00
2 | Stop, 3 hours 0 minutes | Pr. 202 = 0, 0, 3:00
3 | Reverse rotation, 30Hz, 4 hours 0minutes | Pr. 203 = 2, 30, 4:00
4 | Forward rotation, 10Hz, 6 hours 0minutes | Pr. 204 = 1, 10, 6:00
5 | Forward rotation, 35Hz, 7 hours 30minutes | Pr.
205 = 1, 35, 7:30
6 | Stop, 9 hours 0 minutes | Pr. 206 = 0, 0, 9:00
--[p313]-- (Example: Set point No. 1, forward rotation, 30Hz, 4 hours 30 minutes)
1) Read Pr. 201 value.
2) Enter "1" (forward rotation) in Pr. 201 and press the [SET] key ([WRITE] key when using the FR-PU04 parameter unit).
3) Enter 30 (30Hz) and press the [SET] key ([WRITE] key when using the FR-PU04 parameter unit). (Note 1)

===== [p493-493] PAMUX USER’S GUIDE > Jumpers 0–4 (Address) (2块) =====
--[p493]-- Refer to Table 2-5 on the following page to determine how to set the base address of the B5.
Note: That each Pamux station on a bus must have a unique address.
--[p493]-- Jumpers 0–4 (Address)
These jumpers configure the base address of the B5. Since the brain board controls 16 points of I/O, while the Pamux data bus is only eight bits wide, the B5 must be accessed as two consecutive banks of eight I/O channels each. The least significant bit of the Pamux address bus is used to select which bank is accessed (0 = low bank, 1 = high bank). The other 5 bits of the Pamux bus address determine which Pamux station is active.

===== [p262-319] Pr. 73 "0-5V/0-10V selection" > CAUTION (7块) =====
--[p319]-- To ensure accurate positioning at the upper limit etc of a lift, stop-on-contact control causes a mechanical brake to be closed while the motor is developing a holding torque to keep the load in contact with a mechanical stopper etc.
This function suppresses vibration which is liable to occur when the load is stopped upon contact in vertical motion applications, ensuring steady precise positioning
--[p301]-- CAUTION
The zero current detection level setting should not be too high, and the zero current detection time setting not be too long. Otherwise, the detection signal may not be output when torque is not generated at a low output current.
To prevent the machine and equipment from resulting in hazardous conditions by use of the zero current detection signal, install a safety backup such as an emergency brake.
Pr. 154 → Refer to Pr. 22.
--[p319]-- 270 | 0 | 0 | Without stop-on-contact control and load torque high-speed frequency control
1 | Stop-on-contact control

--[p319]-- Load torque high-speed frequency control automatically sets the maximum operating frequency according to the load.

--[p471]-- Noisy applications are better suited to I/O systems that offer greater noise immunity, such as Opto†22ís Mistic and Optomux systems.

--[p468]-- Opto 22 provides bi-directional data exchange software for integrating manufacturing data into the Enterprise Market, software-driven control solutions for the Systems Market, hardware and drivers for the Components Market, and Vertical Market solutions for the water, energy, and semiconductor industries.
All Opto 22 products are manufactured in the U.S. at the companyís headquarters in Temecula, California, and are sold through a global network of distributors, system integrators, and OEMs.
--[p470]-- Pamux is a high-speed, high-density distributed I/O system that accommodates both digital and analog brain boards and I/O modules. A Pamux bus can extend up to 500 feet from a host computer or other programming device.
Pamux supports up to 32 distributable stations containing up to 512 I/O points. Each station is composed of a Pamux brain board and an I/O mounting rack; the final station on the Pamux bus must also include a terminator board.
--[p471]-- The host computer can also access 16 analog input points in under six milliseconds and 16 analog output points in about 15 milliseconds.
The Pamux product line is ideal for low-noise applications, such as:
ï Robotics
ï Numerical control
ï Conveyor line control
ï Sequence-of-events fault detection
Because it is an external high-speed parallel I/O system, Pamux is better suited to environments with low electromagnetic or radio frequency interference.

===== [p198-198] Humphrey VACUUM VALVES > 2.3.3 Inverter-generated noises and reduction techniques (2块) =====
--[p198]-- If these noises cause peripheral devices to misoperate, measures should be taken to suppress the noise. The measures differ slightly depending on noise propagation paths.
--[p198]-- 2.3.3 Inverter-generated noises and reduction techniques
Some noises enter the inverter causing it to misoperate and others are radiated by the inverter causing misoperation of peripheral devices. Though the inverter is designed to be insusceptible to noise, it handles low-level signals, so it requires the following basic measures to be taken. Also, since the inverter chops the output at a high carrier frequency, it could generate noise.

--[p174]-- When two or more inverters are installed or a ventilation fan is mounted in an enclosure, the inverters and ventilation fan must be installed in proper positions with extreme care taken to keep the ambient temperatures of the inverters below the permissible value.
